AEROM_ALT_ABORT.desc: Maximum allowable loss in altitude during a trick or sequence from its starting altitude.
AEROM_ALT_ABORT.name: Altitude Abort

AEROM_ANG_TC.desc: This is the time over which we filter the desired roll to smooth it
AEROM_ANG_TC.name: Roll control filtertime constant

AEROM_DEBUG.desc: This controls the printing of extra debug information on paths
AEROM_DEBUG.name: Debug control

AEROM_ENTRY_RATE.desc: This controls how rapidly we roll into a new orientation
AEROM_ENTRY_RATE.name: The roll rate to use when entering a roll maneuver

AEROM_ERR_COR_D.desc: This controls how rapidly we correct back onto the desired path
AEROM_ERR_COR_D.name: D gain for path error corrections

AEROM_ERR_COR_P.desc: This controls how rapidly we correct back onto the desired path
AEROM_ERR_COR_P.name: P gain for path error corrections

AEROM_KE_RUDD.desc: Percent of rudder normally uses to sustain knife-edge at trick speed
AEROM_KE_RUDD.name: KnifeEdge Rudder

AEROM_KE_RUDD_LK.desc: Time to look ahead in the path to calculate rudder correction for bank angle
AEROM_KE_RUDD_LK.name: KnifeEdge Rudder lookahead

AEROM_LKAHD.desc: This is how much time to look ahead in the path for calculating path rates
AEROM_LKAHD.name: Lookahead

AEROM_MIS_ANGLE.desc: When set to a non-zero value, this is the assumed direction of the mission. Otherwise the waypoint angle is used
AEROM_MIS_ANGLE.name: Mission angle

AEROM_PATH_SCALE.desc: Scale factor for Path/Box size. 0.5 would half the distances in maneuvers. Radii are unaffected.
AEROM_PATH_SCALE.name: Path Scale

AEROM_ROL_COR_TC.desc: This is the time constant for correcting roll errors. A smaller value leads to faster roll corrections
AEROM_ROL_COR_TC.name: Roll control time constant

AEROM_SPD_I.desc: This controls how rapidly the throttle is raised to compensate for a speed error
AEROM_SPD_I.name: I gain for speed controller

AEROM_SPD_P.desc: This controls how rapidly the throttle is raised to compensate for a speed error
AEROM_SPD_P.name: P gain for speed controller

AEROM_STALL_PIT.desc: Pitch threashold for moving to final stage of stall turn
AEROM_STALL_PIT.name: Stall turn pitch threshold

AEROM_STALL_THR.desc: Amount of throttle to reduce to for a stall turn
AEROM_STALL_THR.name: Stall turn throttle

AEROM_THR_BOOST.desc: This is the extra throttle added in schedule elements marked as needing a throttle boost
AEROM_THR_BOOST.name: Throttle boost

AEROM_THR_LKAHD.desc: This controls how far ahead we look in time along the path for the target throttle
AEROM_THR_LKAHD.name: The lookahead for throttle control

AEROM_THR_PIT_FF.desc: This controls how much extra throttle to add based on pitch ange. The value is for 90 degrees and is applied in proportion to pitch
AEROM_THR_PIT_FF.name: Throttle feed forward from pitch

AEROM_TIME_COR_P.desc: This is the time constant for correcting path position errors
AEROM_TIME_COR_P.name: Time constant for correction of our distance along the path

AEROM_TS_I.desc: This controls how rapidly two aircraft are brought back into time sync
AEROM_TS_I.name: Timesync I gain

AEROM_TS_P.desc: This controls how rapidly two aircraft are brought back into time sync
AEROM_TS_P.name: Timesync P gain

AEROM_TS_RATE.desc: This sets the rate we send data for time sync between aircraft
AEROM_TS_RATE.name: Timesync rate of send of NAMED_VALUE_FLOAT data

AEROM_TS_SPDMAX.desc: This sets the maximum speed adjustment for time sync between aircraft
AEROM_TS_SPDMAX.name: Timesync speed max

AEROM_YAW_ACCEL.desc: This is maximum yaw acceleration to use
AEROM_YAW_ACCEL.name: Yaw acceleration

AFS_AMSL_ERR_GPS.desc: This sets margin for error in GPS derived altitude limit. This error margin is only used if the barometer has failed. If the barometer fails then the GPS will be used to enforce the AMSL_LIMIT, but this margin will be subtracted from the AMSL_LIMIT first, to ensure that even with the given amount of GPS altitude error the pressure altitude is not breached. OBC users should set this to comply with their D2 safety case. A value of -1 will mean that barometer failure will lead to immediate termination.
AFS_AMSL_ERR_GPS.name: Error margin for GPS based AMSL limit

AFS_AMSL_LIMIT.desc: This sets the AMSL (above mean sea level) altitude limit. If the pressure altitude determined by QNH exceeds this limit then flight termination will be forced. Note that this limit is in meters, whereas pressure altitude limits are often quoted in feet. A value of zero disables the pressure altitude limit.
AFS_AMSL_LIMIT.name: AMSL limit

AFS_DUAL_LOSS.desc: This enables the dual loss termination part of the AFS system. If this parameter is 1 and both GPS and the ground control station fail simultaneously, this will be considered a "dual loss" and cause termination.
AFS_DUAL_LOSS.name: Enable dual loss terminate due to failure of both GCS and GPS simultaneously

AFS_ENABLE.desc: This enables the advanced failsafe system. If this is set to zero (disable) then all the other AFS options have no effect
AFS_ENABLE.name: Enable Advanced Failsafe

AFS_GCS_TIMEOUT.desc: The time (in seconds) of persistent data link loss before GCS failsafe occurs.
AFS_GCS_TIMEOUT.name: GCS timeout

AFS_GEOFENCE.desc: This enables the geofence part of the AFS. Will only be in effect if AFS_ENABLE is also 1
AFS_GEOFENCE.name: Enable geofence Advanced Failsafe

AFS_GPS_LOSS.desc: Waypoint number to navigate to on GPS lock loss
AFS_GPS_LOSS.name: GPS Loss Waypoint

AFS_HB_PIN.desc: This sets a digital output pin which is cycled at 10Hz when termination is not activated. Note that if a FS_TERM_PIN is set then the heartbeat pin will continue to cycle at 10Hz when termination is activated, to allow the termination board to distinguish between autopilot crash and termination.
AFS_HB_PIN.name: Heartbeat Pin

AFS_HB_PIN.desc: This sets a digital output pin which is cycled at 10Hz when termination is not activated. Note that if a FS_TERM_PIN is set then the heartbeat pin will continue to cycle at 10Hz when termination is activated, to allow the termination board to distinguish between autopilot crash and termination. Some common values are given, but see the Wiki's "GPIOs" page for how to determine the pin number for a given autopilot.
AFS_HB_PIN.name: Heartbeat Pin

AFS_HB_PIN.desc: This sets a digital output pin which is cycled at 10Hz when termination is not activated. Note that if a FS_TERM_PIN is set then the heartbeat pin will continue to cycle at 10Hz when termination is activated, to allow the termination board to distinguish between autopilot crash and termination. Some common values are given, but see the Wiki's "GPIOs" page for how to determine the pin number for a given autopilot.
AFS_HB_PIN.name: Heartbeat Pin

AFS_MAN_PIN.desc: This sets a digital output pin to set high when in manual mode
AFS_MAN_PIN.name: Manual Pin

AFS_MAN_PIN.desc: This sets a digital output pin to set high when in manual mode. See the Wiki's "GPIOs" page for how to determine the pin number for a given autopilot.
AFS_MAN_PIN.name: Manual Pin

AFS_MAX_COM_LOSS.desc: Maximum number of comms loss events before the aircraft stops returning to mission on comms recovery. Use zero to allow for any number of comms loss events.
AFS_MAX_COM_LOSS.name: Maximum number of comms loss events

AFS_MAX_GPS_LOSS.desc: Maximum number of GPS loss events before the aircraft stops returning to mission on GPS recovery. Use zero to allow for any number of GPS loss events.
AFS_MAX_GPS_LOSS.name: Maximum number of GPS loss events

AFS_MAX_RANGE.desc: This is the maximum range of the vehicle in kilometers from first arming. If the vehicle goes beyond this range then the TERM_ACTION is performed. A value of zero disables this feature.
AFS_MAX_RANGE.name: Max allowed range

bits: Continue the mission even after comms are recovered (does not go to the mission item at the time comms were lost)
Enable AFS for all autonomous modes (not just AUTO)
AFS_OPTIONS.desc: See description for each bitmask bit description
AFS_OPTIONS.name: AFS options

bits: Continue the mission even after comms are recovered (does not go to the mission item at the time comms were lost)
Enable AFS for all autonomous modes (not just AUTO)
Option to not jump to AFS_WP_COMMS if already in the return path
AFS_OPTIONS.desc: See description for each bitmask bit description
AFS_OPTIONS.name: AFS options

AFS_QNH_PRESSURE.desc: This sets the QNH pressure in millibars to be used for pressure altitude in the altitude limit. A value of zero disables the altitude limit.
AFS_QNH_PRESSURE.name: QNH pressure

AFS_QNH_PRESSURE.desc: This sets the QNH pressure in millibars to be used for pressure altitude in the altitude limit. A value of zero disables the altitude limit.
AFS_QNH_PRESSURE.name: QNH pressure

AFS_RC.desc: This enables the RC part of the AFS. Will only be in effect if AFS_ENABLE is also 1
AFS_RC.name: Enable RC Advanced Failsafe

AFS_RC_FAIL_TIME.desc: This is the time in seconds in manual mode that failsafe termination will activate if RC input is lost. For the OBC rules this should be (1.5). Use 0 to disable.
AFS_RC_FAIL_TIME.name: RC failure time

AFS_RC_MAN_ONLY.desc: If this parameter is set to 1, then an RC loss will only cause the plane to terminate in manual control modes. If it is 0, then the plane will terminate in any flight mode.
AFS_RC_MAN_ONLY.name: Enable RC Termination only in manual control modes

AFS_TERMINATE.desc: Can be set in flight to force termination of the heartbeat signal
AFS_TERMINATE.name: Force Terminate

AFS_TERM_ACTION.desc: This can be used to force an action on flight termination. Normally this is handled by an external failsafe board, but you can setup APM to handle it here. Please consult the wiki for more information on the possible values of the parameter
AFS_TERM_ACTION.name: Terminate action

AFS_TERM_ACTION.desc: This can be used to force an action on flight termination. Normally this is handled by an external failsafe board, but you can setup ArduPilot to handle it here. Please consult the wiki for more information on the possible values of the parameter
AFS_TERM_ACTION.name: Terminate action

AFS_TERM_PIN.desc: This sets a digital output pin to set high on flight termination
AFS_TERM_PIN.name: Terminate Pin

AFS_TERM_PIN.desc: This sets a digital output pin to set high on flight termination. Some common values are given, but see the Wiki's "GPIOs" page for how to determine the pin number for a given autopilot.
AFS_TERM_PIN.name: Terminate Pin

AFS_TERM_PIN.desc: This sets a digital output pin to set high on flight termination. Some common values are given, but see the Wiki's "GPIOs" page for how to determine the pin number for a given autopilot.
AFS_TERM_PIN.name: Terminate Pin

AFS_WP_COMMS.desc: Waypoint number to navigate to on comms loss
AFS_WP_COMMS.name: Comms Waypoint

AFS_WP_GPS_LOSS.desc: Waypoint number to navigate to on GPS lock loss
AFS_WP_GPS_LOSS.name: GPS Loss Waypoint

AHRS_COMP_BETA.desc: This controls the time constant for the cross-over frequency used to fuse AHRS (airspeed and heading) and GPS data to estimate ground velocity. Time constant is 0.1/beta. A larger time constant will use GPS data less and a small time constant will use air data less.
AHRS_COMP_BETA.name: AHRS Velocity Complementary Filter Beta Coefficient

AHRS_CUSTOM_PIT.desc: Autopilot mounting position pitch offset. Positive values = pitch up, negative values = pitch down. This parameter is only used when AHRS_ORIENTATION is set to CUSTOM.
AHRS_CUSTOM_PIT.name: Board orientation pitch offset

AHRS_CUSTOM_ROLL.desc: Autopilot mounting position roll offset. Positive values = roll right, negative values = roll left. This parameter is only used when AHRS_ORIENTATION is set to CUSTOM.
AHRS_CUSTOM_ROLL.name: Board orientation roll offset

AHRS_CUSTOM_YAW.desc: Autopilot mounting position yaw offset. Positive values = yaw right, negative values = yaw left. This parameter is only used when AHRS_ORIENTATION is set to CUSTOM.
AHRS_CUSTOM_YAW.name: Board orientation yaw offset

AHRS_EKF_TYPE.desc: This controls which NavEKF Kalman filter version is used for attitude and position estimation
AHRS_EKF_TYPE.name: Use NavEKF Kalman filter for attitude and position estimation

AHRS_EKF_TYPE.desc: This controls which NavEKF Kalman filter version is used for attitude and position estimation
AHRS_EKF_TYPE.name: Use NavEKF Kalman filter for attitude and position estimation

AHRS_EKF_TYPE.desc: This controls which NavEKF Kalman filter version is used for attitude and position estimation
AHRS_EKF_TYPE.name: Use NavEKF Kalman filter for attitude and position estimation

AHRS_GPS_GAIN.desc: This controls how much to use the GPS to correct the attitude. This should never be set to zero for a plane as it would result in the plane losing control in turns. For a plane please use the default value of 1.0.
AHRS_GPS_GAIN.name: AHRS GPS gain

AHRS_GPS_MINSATS.desc: Minimum number of satellites visible to use GPS for velocity based corrections attitude correction. This defaults to 6, which is about the point at which the velocity numbers from a GPS become too unreliable for accurate correction of the accelerometers.
AHRS_GPS_MINSATS.name: AHRS GPS Minimum satellites

AHRS_GPS_USE.desc: This controls whether to use dead-reckoning or GPS based navigation. If set to 0 then the GPS won't be used for navigation, and only dead reckoning will be used. A value of zero should never be used for normal flight. Currently this affects only the DCM-based AHRS: the EKF uses GPS whenever it is available.
AHRS_GPS_USE.name: AHRS use GPS for navigation

AHRS_GPS_USE.desc: This controls whether to use dead-reckoning or GPS based navigation. If set to 0 then the GPS won't be used for navigation, and only dead reckoning will be used. A value of zero should never be used for normal flight. Currently this affects only the DCM-based AHRS: the EKF uses GPS according to its own parameters. A value of 2 means to use GPS for height as well as position - both in DCM estimation and when determining altitude-above-home.
AHRS_GPS_USE.name: AHRS use GPS for DCM navigation and position-down
values: Use GPS for DCM position and height

AHRS_OPTIONS.desc: This controls optional AHRS behaviour. Setting DisableDCMFallbackFW will change the AHRS behaviour for fixed wing aircraft in fly-forward flight to not fall back to DCM when the EKF stops navigating. Setting DisableDCMFallbackVTOL will change the AHRS behaviour for fixed wing aircraft in non fly-forward (VTOL) flight to not fall back to DCM when the EKF stops navigating.
AHRS_OPTIONS.name: Optional AHRS behaviour

AHRS_OPTIONS.desc: This controls optional AHRS behaviour. Setting DisableDCMFallbackFW will change the AHRS behaviour for fixed wing aircraft in fly-forward flight to not fall back to DCM when the EKF stops navigating. Setting DisableDCMFallbackVTOL will change the AHRS behaviour for fixed wing aircraft in non fly-forward (VTOL) flight to not fall back to DCM when the EKF stops navigating. Setting DontDisableAirspeedUsingEKF disables the EKF based innovation check for airspeed consistency
AHRS_OPTIONS.name: Optional AHRS behaviour

AHRS_OPTIONS.desc: This controls optional AHRS behaviour. Setting DisableDCMFallbackFW will change the AHRS behaviour for fixed wing aircraft in fly-forward flight to not fall back to DCM when the EKF stops navigating. Setting DisableDCMFallbackVTOL will change the AHRS behaviour for fixed wing aircraft in non fly-forward (VTOL) flight to not fall back to DCM when the EKF stops navigating. Setting DontDisableAirspeedUsingEKF disables the EKF based innovation check for airspeed consistency. Setting AutoRecordOrigin will auto-save the EKF origin to parameters when it becomes valid.
AHRS_OPTIONS.name: Optional AHRS behaviour

AHRS_ORIENTATION.desc: Overall board orientation relative to the standard orientation for the board type. This rotates the IMU and compass readings to allow the board to be oriented in your vehicle at any 90 or 45 degree angle. This option takes affect on next boot. After changing you will need to re-level your vehicle.
AHRS_ORIENTATION.name: Board Orientation

AHRS_ORIENTATION.desc: Overall board orientation relative to the standard orientation for the board type. This rotates the IMU and compass readings to allow the board to be oriented in your vehicle at any 90 or 45 degree angle. The label for each option is specified in the order of rotations for that orientation. This option takes affect on next boot. After changing you will need to re-level your vehicle.
AHRS_ORIENTATION.name: Board Orientation

AHRS_ORIENTATION.desc: Overall board orientation relative to the standard orientation for the board type. This rotates the IMU and compass readings to allow the board to be oriented in your vehicle at any 90 or 45 degree angle. The label for each option is specified in the order of rotations for that orientation. This option takes affect on next boot. After changing you will need to re-level your vehicle. Firmware versions 4.2 and prior can use a CUSTOM (100) rotation to set the AHRS_CUSTOM_ROLL/PIT/YAW angles for AHRS orientation. Later versions provide two general custom rotations which can be used, Custom 1 and Custom 2, with CUST_ROT1_ROLL/PIT/YAW or CUST_ROT2_ROLL/PIT/YAW angles.
AHRS_ORIENTATION.name: Board Orientation

AHRS_ORIGIN_ALT.desc: AHRS last origin altitude in meters
AHRS_ORIGIN_ALT.name: AHRS last origin altitude

AHRS_ORIGIN_LAT.desc: AHRS last origin latitude in degrees
AHRS_ORIGIN_LAT.name: AHRS last origin latitude

AHRS_ORIGIN_LON.desc: AHRS last origin longitude in degrees
AHRS_ORIGIN_LON.name: AHRS last origin longitude

AHRS_ORIG_ALT.desc: AHRS/EKF origin will be set to this altitude (in meters above sea level) if not already set
AHRS_ORIG_ALT.name: AHRS/EKF Origin Altitude

AHRS_ORIG_LAT.desc: AHRS/EKF origin will be set to this latitude if not already set
AHRS_ORIG_LAT.name: AHRS/EKF Origin Latitude

AHRS_ORIG_LON.desc: AHRS/EKF origin will be set to this longitude if not already set
AHRS_ORIG_LON.name: AHRS/EKF Origin Longitude

AHRS_RP_P.desc: This controls how fast the accelerometers correct the attitude
AHRS_RP_P.name: AHRS RP_P

AHRS_TRIM_X.desc: Compensates for the roll angle difference between the control board and the frame. Positive values make the vehicle roll right.
AHRS_TRIM_X.name: AHRS Trim Roll

AHRS_TRIM_Y.desc: Compensates for the pitch angle difference between the control board and the frame. Positive values make the vehicle pitch up/back.
AHRS_TRIM_Y.name: AHRS Trim Pitch

AHRS_WIND_MAX.desc: This sets the maximum allowable difference between ground speed and airspeed. This allows the plane to cope with a failing airspeed sensor. A value of zero means to use the airspeed as is.
AHRS_WIND_MAX.name: Maximum wind

AHRS_WIND_MAX.desc: This sets the maximum allowable difference between ground speed and airspeed. This allows the plane to cope with a failing airspeed sensor. A value of zero means to use the airspeed as is. See ARSPD_OPTIONS and ARSPD_MAX_WIND to disable airspeed sensors.
AHRS_WIND_MAX.name: Maximum wind

AHRS_WIND_MAX.desc: This sets the maximum allowable difference between ground speed and airspeed. A value of zero means to use the airspeed as is. This allows the plane to cope with a failing airspeed sensor by clipping it to groundspeed plus/minus this limit. See ARSPD_OPTIONS and ARSPD_WIND_MAX to disable airspeed sensors.
AHRS_WIND_MAX.name: Maximum wind

AHRS_YAW_P.desc: This controls the weight the compass or GPS has on the heading. A higher value means the heading will track the yaw source (GPS or compass) more rapidly.
AHRS_YAW_P.name: Yaw P

AIS_LIST_MAX.desc: AIS list size of nearest vessels. Longer lists take longer to refresh with lower SRx_ADSB values.
AIS_LIST_MAX.name: AIS vessel list size

AIS_TIME_OUT.desc: if no updates are received in this time a vessel will be removed from the list
AIS_TIME_OUT.name: AIS vessel time out

ALAND_WP_ALT.desc: Altitude of final approach waypoint created by script
ALAND_WP_ALT.name: Final approach waypoint alt

ALAND_WP_DIST.desc: Distance from landing point (HOME) to final approach waypoint created by script in the opposite direction of initial takeoff
ALAND_WP_DIST.name: Final approach waypoint distance

ARMING_ACCTHRESH.desc: Accelerometer error threshold used to determine inconsistent accelerometers. Compares this error range to other accelerometers to detect a hardware or calibration error. Lower value means tighter check and harder to pass arming check. Not all accelerometers are created equal.
ARMING_ACCTHRESH.name: Accelerometer error threshold

ARMING_CHECK.desc: Checks prior to arming motor. This is a bitmask of checks that will be performed before allowing arming. The default is no checks, allowing arming at any time. You can select whatever checks you prefer by adding together the values of each check type to set this parameter. For example, to only allow arming when you have GPS lock and no RC failsafe you would set ARMING_CHECK to 72. For most users it is recommended that you set this to 1 to enable all checks.
ARMING_CHECK.name: Arm Checks to Peform (bitmask)

ARMING_CHECK.desc: Checks prior to arming motor. This is a bitmask of checks that will be performed before allowing arming. For most users it is recommended to leave this at the default of 1 (all checks enabled). You can select whatever checks you prefer by adding together the values of each check type to set this parameter. For example, to only allow arming when you have GPS lock and no RC failsafe you would set ARMING_CHECK to 72.
ARMING_CHECK.name: Arm Checks to Perform (bitmask)

ARMING_CRSDP_IGN.desc: Must have value "1" if crashdump data is present on the system, or a prearm failure will be raised. Do not set this parameter unless the risks of doing so are fully understood. The presence of a crash dump means that the firmware currently installed has suffered a critical software failure which resulted in the autopilot immediately rebooting. The crashdump file gives diagnostic information which can help in finding the issue, please contact the ArduPIlot support team. If this crashdump data is present, the vehicle is likely unsafe to fly. Check the ArduPilot documentation for more details.
ARMING_CRSDP_IGN.name: Disable CrashDump Arming check

ARMING_MAGTHRESH.desc: Compass magnetic field strength error threshold vs earth magnetic model. X and y axis are compared using this threhold, Z axis uses 2x this threshold. 0 to disable check
ARMING_MAGTHRESH.name: Compass magnetic field strength error threshold vs earth magnetic model

ARMING_MIS_ITEMS.desc: Bitmask of mission items that are required to be planned in order to arm the aircraft
ARMING_MIS_ITEMS.name: Required mission items

ARMING_MIS_ITEMS.desc: Bitmask of mission items that are required to be planned in order to arm the aircraft
ARMING_MIS_ITEMS.name: Required mission items

ARMING_NEED_LOC.desc: Require that the vehicle have an absolute position before it arms. This can help ensure that the vehicle can Return To Launch.
ARMING_NEED_LOC.name: Require vehicle location

ARMING_OPTIONS.desc: Options that can be applied to change arming behaviour
ARMING_OPTIONS.name: Arming options

ARMING_OPTIONS.desc: Options that can be applied to change arming behaviour
ARMING_OPTIONS.name: Arming options
values: Do not send status text on state change

bits: Do not send status text on state change
Skip IMU consistency checks when ICE motor running
ARMING_OPTIONS.desc: Options that can be applied to change arming behaviour
ARMING_OPTIONS.name: Arming options

ARMING_REQUIRE.desc: Arming disabled until some requirements are met. If 0, there are no requirements (arm immediately). If 1, require rudder stick or GCS arming before arming motors and sends the minimum throttle PWM value to the throttle channel when disarmed. If 2, require rudder stick or GCS arming and send 0 PWM to throttle channel when disarmed. See the ARMING_CHECK_* parameters to see what checks are done before arming. Note, if setting this parameter to 0 a reboot is required to arm the plane. Also note, even with this parameter at 0, if ARMING_CHECK parameter is not also zero the plane may fail to arm throttle at boot due to a pre-arm check failure.
ARMING_REQUIRE.name: Require Arming Motors

ARMING_REQUIRE.desc: Arming disabled until some requirements are met. If 0, there are no requirements (arm immediately). If 1, require rudder stick or GCS arming before arming motors and sends the minimum throttle PWM value to the throttle channel when disarmed. If 2, require rudder stick or GCS arming and send 0 PWM to throttle channel when disarmed. See the ARMING_CHECK_* parameters to see what checks are done before arming. Note, if setting this parameter to 0 a reboot is required to arm the plane. Also note, even with this parameter at 0, if ARMING_CHECK parameter is not also zero the plane may fail to arm throttle at boot due to a pre-arm check failure. On planes with ICE enabled and the throttle while disarmed option set in ICE_OPTIONS the motor will get THR_MIN when disarmed.
ARMING_REQUIRE.name: Require Arming Motors

ARMING_REQUIRE.desc: Arming disabled until some requirements are met. If 0, there are no requirements (arm immediately). If 1, sends the minimum throttle PWM value to the throttle channel when disarmed. If 2, send 0 PWM (no signal) to throttle channel when disarmed. On planes with ICE enabled and the throttle while disarmed option set in ICE_OPTIONS, the motor will always get THR_MIN when disarmed. Arming will occur using either rudder stick arming (if enabled) or GCS command when all mandatory and ARMING_CHECK items are satisfied. Note, when setting this parameter to 0, a reboot is required to immediately arm the plane.
ARMING_REQUIRE.name: Require Arming Motors

ARMING_REQUIRE.desc: Arming disabled until some requirements are met. If 0, there are no requirements (arm immediately). If 1, all checks not skipped by ARMING_SKIPCHK must pass before the vehicle can be armed (for example, via rudder stick or GCS command). If 3, Arm immediately once pre-arm/arm checks are satisfied, but only one time per boot up. Note that a reboot is NOT required when setting to 0 but IS require when setting to 3.
ARMING_REQUIRE.name: Require Arming Motors

ARMING_RUDDER.desc: Allow arm/disarm by rudder input. When enabled arming can be done with right rudder, disarming with left rudder. Rudder arming only works in manual throttle modes with throttle at zero +- deadzone (RCx_DZ)
ARMING_RUDDER.name: Arming with Rudder enable/disable

ARMING_RUDDER.desc: Allow arm/disarm by rudder input. When enabled arming can be done with right rudder, disarming with left rudder. Rudder arming only works with throttle at zero +- deadzone (RCx_DZ). Depending on vehicle type, arming in certain modes is prevented. See the wiki for each vehicle. Caution is recommended when arming if it is allowed in an auto-throttle mode!
ARMING_RUDDER.name: Arming with Rudder enable/disable

ARMING_SKIPCHK.desc: Checks to skip prior to arming motor. This is a bitmask of checks before allowing arming that will be skipped. For most users it is recommended to leave this at the default of 0 (no checks skipped). In extreme circumstances, a value of -1 can be used to skip all non-mandatory current and future checks.
ARMING_SKIPCHK.name: Arm Checks to Skip (bitmask)

ARM_C_RTL_ALT.desc: RTL_ALT should be < 120m (400ft). 3 or less to prevent arming. -1 to disable.
ARM_C_RTL_ALT.name: RTL_ALT should be a valid value

ARM_C_RTL_ALT_M.desc: RTL_ALT_M should be < 120m (400ft). 3 or less to prevent arming. -1 to disable.
ARM_C_RTL_ALT_M.name: RTL_ALT_M should be a valid value

ARM_ESTOP.desc: Emergency Stop disables arming. 3 or less to prevent arming. -1 to disable.
ARM_ESTOP.name: Motors EStopped

ARM_FENCE.desc: Fences loaded but no fence enabled. 3 or less to prevent arming. -1 to disable.
ARM_FENCE.name: Fence not enabled

ARM_FOLL_OFS_DEF.desc: Follow offsets should not be left as default (zero) if FOLL_ENABLE = 1. 3 or less to prevent arming. -1 to disable.
ARM_FOLL_OFS_DEF.name: Follow Offsets defaulted

ARM_FOLL_SYSID.desc: If FOLL_ENABLE = 1, check that FOLL_SYSID has been set. 3 or less to prevent arming. -1 to disable.
ARM_FOLL_SYSID.name: FOLL_SYSID must be set

ARM_FOLL_SYSID_X.desc: If FOLL_ENABLE = 1, check that FOLL_SYSID is different to MAV_SYSID. 3 or less to prevent arming. -1 to disable.
ARM_FOLL_SYSID_X.name: Vehicle should not follow itself

ARSPD2_TUBE_ORDR.desc: This parameter allows you to control whether the order in which the tubes are attached to your pitot tube matters. If you set this to 0 then the top connector on the sensor needs to be the dynamic pressure. If set to 1 then the bottom connector needs to be the dynamic pressure. If set to 2 (the default) then the airspeed driver will accept either order. The reason you may wish to specify the order is it will allow your airspeed sensor to detect if the aircraft it receiving excessive pressure on the static port, which would otherwise be seen as a positive airspeed.
ARSPD2_TUBE_ORDR.name: Control pitot tube order of 2nd airspeed sensor

ARSPD2_TUBE_ORDR.desc: This parameter allows you to control whether the order in which the tubes are attached to your pitot tube matters. If you set this to 0 then the first (often the top) connector on the sensor needs to be the stagnation pressure (the pressure at the tip of the pitot tube). If set to 1 then the second (often the bottom) connector needs to be the stagnation pressure. If set to 2 (the default) then the airspeed driver will accept either order. The reason you may wish to specify the order is it will allow your airspeed sensor to detect if the aircraft is receiving excessive pressure on the static port compared to the stagnation port such as during a stall, which would otherwise be seen as a positive airspeed.
ARSPD2_TUBE_ORDR.name: Control pitot tube order of 2nd airspeed sensor

BARO_ALTERR_MAX.desc: This is the maximum acceptable altitude discrepancy between GPS altitude and barometric presssure altitude calculated against a standard atmosphere for arming checks to pass. If you are getting an arming error due to this parameter then you may have a faulty or substituted barometer. A common issue is vendors replacing a MS5611 in a "Pixhawk" with a MS5607. If you have that issue then please see BARO_OPTIONS parameter to force the MS5611 to be treated as a MS5607. This check is disabled if the value is zero.
BARO_ALTERR_MAX.name: Altitude error maximum

BARO_ALT_OFFSET.desc: altitude offset in meters added to barometric altitude. This is used to allow for automatic adjustment of the base barometric altitude by a ground station equipped with a barometer. The value is added to the barometric altitude read by the aircraft. It is automatically reset to 0 when the barometer is calibrated on each reboot or when a preflight calibration is performed.
BARO_ALT_OFFSET.name: altitude offset

BARO_EXT_BUS.desc: This selects the bus number for looking for an I2C barometer. When set to -1 it will probe all external i2c buses based on the GND_PROBE_EXT parameter.
BARO_EXT_BUS.name: External baro bus

BARO_EXT_BUS.desc: This selects the bus number for looking for an I2C barometer. When set to -1 it will probe all external i2c buses based on the BARO_PROBE_EXT parameter.
BARO_EXT_BUS.name: External baro bus

BARO_FIELD_ELV.desc: User provided field elevation in meters. This is used to improve the calculation of the altitude the vehicle is at. This parameter is not persistent and will be reset to 0 every time the vehicle is rebooted. Changes to this parameter will only be used when disarmed. A value of 0 means the EKF origin height is used for takeoff height above sea level.
BARO_FIELD_ELV.name: field elevation

BARO_FLTR_RNG.desc: This sets the range around the average value that new samples must be within to be accepted. This can help reduce the impact of noise on sensors that are on long I2C cables. The value is a percentage from the average value. A value of zero disables this filter.
BARO_FLTR_RNG.name: Range in which sample is accepted

BARO_GND_TEMP.desc: User provided ambient ground temperature in degrees Celsius. This is used to improve the calculation of the altitude the vehicle is at. This parameter is not persistent and will be reset to 0 every time the vehicle is rebooted. A value of 0 means use the internal measurement ambient temperature.
BARO_GND_TEMP.name: ground temperature

BARO_PRIMARY.desc: This selects which barometer will be the primary if multiple barometers are found
BARO_PRIMARY.name: Primary barometer

BARO_PROBE_EXT.desc: This sets which types of external i2c barometer to look for. It is a bitmask of barometer types. The I2C buses to probe is based on GND_EXT_BUS. If BARO_EXT_BUS is -1 then it will probe all external buses, otherwise it will probe just the bus number given in GND_EXT_BUS.
BARO_PROBE_EXT.name: External barometers to probe

BARO_PROBE_EXT.desc: This sets which types of external i2c barometer to look for. It is a bitmask of barometer types. The I2C buses to probe is based on BARO_EXT_BUS. If BARO_EXT_BUS is -1 then it will probe all external buses, otherwise it will probe just the bus number given in BARO_EXT_BUS.

BARO_SPEC_GRAV.desc: This sets the specific gravity of the fluid when flying an underwater ROV.
BARO_SPEC_GRAV.name: Specific Gravity (For water depth measurement)

BARO_THST_FILT.desc: Low-pass filter cutoff frequency for thrust compensation. This smooths the throttle input to prevent rapid baro altitude changes during throttle transients. Set to 0 to disable filtering.
BARO_THST_FILT.name: Thrust compensation filter cutoff

BATT2_AMP_OFFSET.desc: Voltage offset at zero current on current sensor
BATT2_AMP_OFFSET.name: AMP offset

BATT2_AMP_OFFSET.desc: Voltage offset at zero current on current sensor for Analog Sensors. For Synthetic Current sensor, this offset is the zero throttle system current and is added to the calculated throttle base current.
BATT2_AMP_OFFSET.name: AMP offset

BATT2_AMP_PERVLT.desc: Number of amps that a 1V reading on the current sensor corresponds to. With a Pixhawk using the 3DR Power brick this should be set to 17. For the Pixhawk with the 3DR 4in1 ESC this should be 17.
BATT2_AMP_PERVLT.name: Amps per volt

BATT2_AMP_PERVLT.name: Amps per volt

BATT2_ARM_MAH.desc: Battery capacity remaining which is required to arm the aircraft. Set to 0 to allow arming at any capacity. Note that execept for smart batteries rebooting the vehicle will always reset the remaining capacity estimate, which can lead to this check not providing sufficent protection, it is recommended to always use this in conjunction with the BATT2__ARM_VOLT parameter.
BATT2_ARM_MAH.name: Required arming remaining capacity

BATT2_CRT_MAH.desc: Battery capacity at which the critical battery failsafe is triggered. Set to 0 to disable battery remaining failsafe. If the battery capacity drops below this level the vehicle will perform the failsafe specified by the BATT2__FS_CRT_ACT parameter.
BATT2_CRT_MAH.name: Battery critical capacity

BATT2_CRT_VOLT.name: Critical battery voltage

BATT2_CURR_MULT.desc: Multiplier applied to all current related reports to allow for adjustment if no UAVCAN param access or current splitting applications
BATT2_CURR_MULT.name: Scales reported power monitor current

BATT2_CURR_PIN.desc: Sets the analog input pin that should be used for current monitoring.

BATT2_FL_FLTR.desc: Filter frequency in Hertz where a low pass filter is used. This is used to filter out tank slosh from the fuel level reading. A value of -1 disables the filter and unfiltered voltage is used to determine the fuel level. The suggested values at in the range of 0.2 Hz to 0.5 Hz.
BATT2_FL_FLTR.name: Fuel level filter frequency

BATT2_FL_PIN.desc: Analog input pin that fuel level sensor is connected to. Airspeed ports can be used for Analog input. When using analog pin 103, the maximum value of the input in 3.3V.

BATT2_FL_PIN.desc: Analog input pin that fuel level sensor is connected to.Analog Airspeed or RSSI ports can be used for Analog input( some autopilots provide others also). Values for some autopilots are given as examples. Search wiki for "Analog pins".

BATT2_FL_VLT_MIN.desc: The voltage seen on the analog pin when the fuel tank is empty. Note: For this type of battery monitor, the voltage seen by the analog pin is displayed as battery voltage on a GCS.
BATT2_FL_VLT_MIN.name: Empty fuel level voltage

BATT2_FL_V_MULT.desc: Voltage multiplier to determine what the full tank voltage reading is. This is calculated as 1 / (Voltage_Full - Voltage_Empty) Note: For this type of battery monitor, the voltage seen by the analog pin is displayed as battery voltage on a GCS.
BATT2_FL_V_MULT.name: Fuel level voltage multiplier

BATT2_LOW_TIMER.desc: This is the timeout in seconds before a low voltage event will be triggered. For aircraft with low C batteries it may be necessary to raise this in order to cope with low voltage on long takeoffs. A value of zero disables low voltage errors.

BRD_SAFETYENABLE.desc: This controls the default state of the safety switch at startup. When set to 1 the safety switch will start in the safe state (flashing) at boot. When set to zero the safety switch will start in the unsafe state (solid) at startup. Note that if a safety switch is fitted the user can still control the safety state after startup using the switch. The safety state can also be controlled in software using a MAVLink message.
BRD_SAFETYENABLE.name: Enable use of safety arming switch

bits: Force safety on when the aircraft disarms
BRD_SAFETYOPTION.desc: This controls the activation of the safety button. It allows you to control if the safety button can be used for safety enable and/or disable, and whether the button is only active when disarmed
BRD_SAFETYOPTION.name: Options for safety button behavior

bits: Force safety on when the aircraft disarms
BRD_SAFETYOPTION.desc: This controls the activation of the safety button. It allows you to control if the safety button can be used for safety enable and/or disable, and whether the button is only active when disarmed
BRD_SAFETYOPTION.name: Options for safety button behavior

BRD_SAFETY_DEFLT.desc: This controls the default state of the safety switch at startup. When set to 1 the safety switch will start in the safe state (flashing) at boot. BRD_SAFETY_DEFLT.name: Sets default state of the safety switch

BRD_SAFETY_MASK.desc: A bitmask which controls what channels can move while the safety switch has not been pressed
BRD_SAFETY_MASK.name: Channels which ignore the safety switch state

BRD_SD_FENCE.desc: This sets the amount of storage in kilobytes reserved on the microsd card in fence.stg for fence storage.
BRD_SD_FENCE.name: SDCard Fence size

BRD_SD_MISSION.desc: This sets the amount of storage in kilobytes reserved on the microsd card in mission.stg for waypoint storage. Each waypoint uses 15 bytes.
BRD_SD_MISSION.name: SDCard Mission size

BRD_SD_SLOWDOWN.desc: This is a scaling factor to slow down microSD operation. It can be used on flight board and microSD card combinations where full speed is not reliable. For normal full speed operation a value of 0 should be used.
BRD_SD_SLOWDOWN.name: microSD slowdown

BRD_SER1_RTSCTS.desc: Enable flow control on serial 1 (telemetry 1) on Pixhawk. You must have the RTS and CTS pins connected to your radio. CAM1_COMPID.desc: Component ID of the camera when using MAVLinkCamV2 (CAMn_TYPE=6). Zero selects MAV_COMP_ID_CAMERA plus the zero-based camera instance (100 for camera 1, 101 for camera 2). Values 7 to 255 select the specified component ID. IDs 1 to 6 are reserved for autopilot-connected cameras.
CAM1_COMPID.name: MAVLink camera component ID

CAM1_FEEDBAK_PIN.desc: pin number to use for save accurate camera feedback messages. If set to -1 then don't use a pin flag for this, otherwise this is a pin number which if held high after a picture trigger order, will save camera messages when camera really takes a picture. A universal camera hot shoe is needed. The pin should be held high for at least 2 milliseconds for reliable trigger detection. Some common values are given, but see the Wiki's "GPIOs" page for how to determine the pin number for a given autopilot. See also the CAMx_FEEDBCK_POL option.
CAM1_FEEDBAK_PIN.name: Camera feedback pin

DR_NEXT_MODE.desc: Copter switch to this mode after GPS recovers or DR_FLY_TIMEOUT has elapsed. Default is 6/RTL. Set to -1 to return to mode used before deadreckoning was triggered
DR_NEXT_MODE.name: Deadreckoning Next Mode

bits: Vector Nav use uncompensated values for accel gyro and mag.
EAHRS_OPTIONS.name: External AHRS options

bits: Vector Nav use uncompensated values for accel gyro and mag
EAHRS_OPTIONS.name: External AHRS options

EFI_2K_CANDRV.desc: NMEA 2000 CAN driver. Use 1 for first CAN scripting driver, 2 for 2nd driver
EFI_2K_CANDRV.name: NMEA 2000 CAN driver

EFI_COEF1.desc: Used to calibrate fuel flow for MS protocol (Slope)
EFI_COEF1.name: EFI Calibration Coefficient 1

EFI_COEF1.desc: Used to calibrate fuel flow for MS protocol (Slope). This should be calculated from a log at constant fuel usage rate. Plot (ECYL[0].InjT*EFI.Rpm)/600.0 to get the duty_cycle. Measure actual fuel usage in cm^3/min, and set EFI_COEF1 = fuel_usage_cm3permin / duty_cycle
EFI_COEF1.name: EFI Calibration Coefficient 1

EFI_COEF2.desc: Used to calibrate fuel flow for MS protocol (Offset)
EFI_COEF2.name: EFI Calibration Coefficient 2

EFI_COEF2.desc: Used to calibrate fuel flow for MS protocol (Offset). This can be used to correct for a non-zero offset in the fuel consumption calculation of EFI_COEF1
EFI_COEF2.name: EFI Calibration Coefficient 2

EFI_DLA_LPS.desc: EFI DLA litres of fuel per second of injection time
EFI_DLA_LPS.name: EFI DLA fuel scale

EFI_H6K_CANDRV.desc: Halo6000 CAN driver. Use 1 for first CAN scripting driver, 2 for 2nd driver
EFI_H6K_CANDRV.name: Halo6000 CAN driver

EFI_H6K_FUELTOT.desc: The capacity of the tank in litres
EFI_H6K_FUELTOT.name: Halo6000 total fuel capacity

EFI_H6K_START_FN.desc: The RC auxilliary function number for start/stop of the generator. Zero to disable start function
EFI_H6K_START_FN.name: Halo6000 start auxilliary function

EFI_H6K_TELEM_RT.desc: The rate that additional generator telemetry is sent
EFI_H6K_TELEM_RT.name: Halo6000 telemetry rate

EFI_HFE_ECU_IDX.desc: HFI EFI ECU index, 0 for automatic
EFI_HFE_ECU_IDX.name: HFI EFI ECU index

EFI_HFE_FUEL_DTY.desc: HFI EFI fuel density in gram per litre
EFI_HFE_FUEL_DTY.name: HFI EFI fuel density

EFI_INF_IGN_AUX.desc: EFI INF throttle ignition aux function
EFI_INF_IGN_AUX.name: EFI INF-Inject ignition aux function

EFI_SP_GEN_FN.desc: SkyPower EFI generator control function. This is the RCn_OPTION value to use to find the R/C channel used for controlling generator start/stop
EFI_SP_GEN_FN.name: SkyPower EFI generator control function

EFI_SP_LOG_RT.desc: SkyPower EFI log rate. This is the rate at which extra logging of the SkyPower EFI is performed
EFI_SP_LOG_RT.name: SkyPower EFI log rate

EFI_SP_MIN_RPM.desc: SkyPower EFI minimum RPM. This is the RPM below which the engine is considered to be stopped
EFI_SP_MIN_RPM.name: SkyPower EFI minimum RPM

EFI_SP_RST_TIME.desc: SkyPower EFI restart time. If engine should be running and it has stopped for this amount of time then auto-restart. To disable this feature set this value to zero.
EFI_SP_RST_TIME.name: SkyPower EFI restart time

EFI_SP_START_FN.desc: SkyPower EFI start function. This is the RCn_OPTION value to use to find the R/C channel used for controlling engine start
EFI_SP_START_FN.name: SkyPower EFI start function

EFI_SP_ST_DISARM.desc: SkyPower EFI allow start disarmed. This controls if starting the engine while disarmed is allowed
EFI_SP_ST_DISARM.name: SkyPower EFI allow start disarmed

EFI_SP_THR_FN.desc: SkyPower EFI throttle function. This sets which SERVOn_FUNCTION to use for the target throttle. This should be 70 for fixed wing aircraft and 31 for helicopter rotor speed control
EFI_SP_THR_FN.name: SkyPower EFI throttle function

EFI_SP_THR_RATE.desc: SkyPower EFI throttle rate. This sets rate at which throttle updates are sent to the engine
EFI_SP_THR_RATE.name: SkyPower EFI throttle rate

EFI_SP_TLM_RT.desc: SkyPower EFI telemetry rate. This is the rate at which extra telemetry values are sent to the GCS
EFI_SP_TLM_RT.name: SkyPower EFI telemetry rate

EFI_SVF_ARMCHECK.desc: Check for Generator ARM state before arming
EFI_SVF_ARMCHECK.name: Generator SVFFI arming check

EFI_THRLIN_COEF1.desc: First Order Polynomial Coefficient. (=1, if throttle is first order polynomial trendline)
EFI_THRLIN_COEF1.name: Throttle linearisation - First Order

EFI_THRLIN_COEF2.desc: Second Order Polynomial Coefficient (=0, if throttle is second order polynomial trendline)
EFI_THRLIN_COEF2.name: Throttle linearisation - Second Order

EFI_THRLIN_COEF3.desc: Third Order Polynomial Coefficient. (=0, if throttle is third order polynomial trendline)
EFI_THRLIN_COEF3.name: Throttle linearisation - Third Order

EFI_TYPE.desc: What method of communication is used for EFI #1
EFI_TYPE.name: EFI communication type

EFI_TYPE.desc: What method of communication is used for EFI #1
EFI_TYPE.name: EFI communication type

EFI_TYPE.desc: What method of communication is used for EFI #1
EFI_TYPE.name: EFI communication type
