EFI_TYPE.name: EFI communication type

EFI_TYPE.desc: What method of communication is used for EFI #1
EFI_TYPE.name: EFI communication type

EK2_ABIAS_P_NSE.desc: This noise controls the growth of the vertical accelerometer delta velocity bias state error estimate. Increasing it makes accelerometer bias estimation faster and noisier.
EK2_ABIAS_P_NSE.name: Accelerometer bias stability (m/s^3)

EK2_ACC_P_NSE.desc: This control disturbance noise controls the growth of estimated error due to accelerometer measurement errors excluding bias. Increasing it makes the flter trust the accelerometer measurements less and other measurements more.
EK2_ACC_P_NSE.name: Accelerometer noise (m/s^2)

EK2_ALT_M_NSE.desc: This is the RMS value of noise in the altitude measurement. Increasing it reduces the weighting of the baro measurement and will make the filter respond more slowly to baro measurement errors, but will make it more sensitive to GPS and accelerometer errors.
EK2_ALT_M_NSE.name: Altitude measurement noise (m)

EK2_ALT_SOURCE.desc: Primary height sensor used by the EKF. If the selected option cannot be used, baro is used. 1 uses the range finder and only with optical flow navigation (EK2_GPS_TYPE = 3), Do not use "1" for terrain following. NOTE: the EK2_RNG_USE_HGT parameter can be used to switch to range-finder when close to the ground.
EK2_ALT_SOURCE.name: Primary altitude sensor source

EK2_ALT_SOURCE.desc: Primary height sensor used by the EKF. If a sensor other than Baro is selected and becomes unavailable, then the Baro sensor will be used as a fallback. NOTE: The EK2_RNG_USE_HGT parameter can be used to switch to range-finder when close to the ground in conjunction with EK2_ALT_SOURCE = 0 or 2 (Baro or GPS).
EK2_ALT_SOURCE.name: Primary altitude sensor source

EK2_BCN_DELAY.desc: This is the number of msec that the range beacon measurements lag behind the inertial measurements. It is the time from the end of the optical flow averaging period and does not include the time delay due to the 100msec of averaging within the flow sensor.
EK2_BCN_DELAY.name: Range beacon measurement delay (msec)

EK2_BCN_I_GTE.desc: This sets the percentage number of standard deviations applied to the range beacon measurement innovation consistency check. Decreasing it makes it more likely that good measurements will be rejected. Increasing it makes it more likely that bad measurements will be accepted.
EK2_BCN_I_GTE.name: Range beacon measurement gate size

EK2_BCN_M_NSE.desc: This is the RMS value of noise in the range beacon measurement. Increasing it reduces the weighting on this measurement.
EK2_BCN_M_NSE.name: Range beacon measurement noise (m)

EK2_CHECK_SCALE.desc: This scales the thresholds that are used to check GPS accuracy before it is used by the EKF. A value of 100 is the default. Values greater than 100 increase and values less than 100 reduce the maximum GPS error the EKF will accept. A value of 200 will double the allowable GPS error.
EK2_CHECK_SCALE.name: GPS accuracy check scaler (%)

EK2_EAS_I_GATE.desc: This sets the percentage number of standard deviations applied to the airspeed measurement innovation consistency check. Decreasing it makes it more likely that good measurements will be rejected. Increasing it makes it more likely that bad measurements will be accepted.
EK2_EAS_I_GATE.name: Airspeed measurement gate size

EK2_EAS_M_NSE.desc: This is the RMS value of noise in equivalent airspeed measurements used by planes. Increasing it reduces the weighting of airspeed measurements and will make wind speed estimates less noisy and slower to converge. Increasing also increases navigation errors when dead-reckoning without GPS measurements.
EK2_EAS_M_NSE.name: Equivalent airspeed measurement noise (m/s)

EK2_ENABLE.desc: This enables EKF2. Enabling EKF2 only makes the maths run, it does not mean it will be used for flight control. To use it for flight control set AHRS_EKF_TYPE=2. A reboot or restart will need to be performed after changing the value of EK2_ENABLE for it to take effect.
EK2_ENABLE.name: Enable EKF2

EK2_EXTNAV_DELAY.desc: This is the number of msec that the external navigation system measurements lag behind the inertial measurements.
EK2_EXTNAV_DELAY.name: external navigation system measurement delay (msec)

EK2_FLOW_DELAY.desc: This is the number of msec that the optical flow measurements lag behind the inertial measurements. It is the time from the end of the optical flow averaging period and does not include the time delay due to the 100msec of averaging within the flow sensor.
EK2_FLOW_DELAY.name: Optical Flow measurement delay (msec)

EK2_FLOW_I_GATE.desc: This sets the percentage number of standard deviations applied to the optical flow innovation consistency check. Decreasing it makes it more likely that good measurements will be rejected. Increasing it makes it more likely that bad measurements will be accepted.
EK2_FLOW_I_GATE.name: Optical Flow measurement gate size

EK2_FLOW_M_NSE.desc: This is the RMS value of noise and errors in optical flow measurements. Increasing it reduces the weighting on these measurements.
EK2_FLOW_M_NSE.name: Optical flow measurement noise (rad/s)

EK2_FLOW_USE.desc: Controls if the optical flow data is fused into the 24-state navigation estimator OR the 1-state terrain height estimator.
EK2_FLOW_USE.name: Optical flow use bitmask

EK2_GBIAS_P_NSE.desc: This state process noise controls growth of the gyro delta angle bias state error estimate. Increasing it makes rate gyro bias estimation faster and noisier.
EK2_GBIAS_P_NSE.name: Rate gyro bias stability (rad/s/s)

EK2_GLITCH_RAD.desc: This controls the maximum radial uncertainty in position between the value predicted by the filter and the value measured by the GPS before the filter position and velocity states are reset to the GPS. Making this value larger allows the filter to ignore larger GPS glitches but also means that non-GPS errors such as IMU and compass can create a larger error in position before the filter is forced back to the GPS position.
EK2_GLITCH_RAD.name: GPS glitch radius gate size (m)

EK2_GPS_CHECK.desc: This is a 1 byte bitmap controlling which GPS preflight checks are performed. Set to 0 to bypass all checks. Set to 255 perform all checks. Set to 3 to check just the number of satellites and HDoP. Set to 31 for the most rigorous checks that will still allow checks to pass when the copter is moving, eg launch from a boat.
EK2_GPS_CHECK.name: GPS preflight check

EK2_GPS_TYPE.desc: This controls use of GPS measurements : 0 = use 3D velocity & 2D position, 1 = use 2D velocity and 2D position, 2 = use 2D position, 3 = Inhibit GPS use - this can be useful when flying with an optical flow sensor in an environment where GPS quality is poor and subject to large multipath errors.
EK2_GPS_TYPE.name: GPS mode control

EK2_GSCL_P_NSE.desc: This noise controls the rate of gyro scale factor learning. Increasing it makes rate gyro scale factor estimation faster and noisier.
EK2_GSCL_P_NSE.name: Rate gyro scale factor stability (1/s)

EK2_GSF_RST_MAX.desc: Sets the maximum number of times the EKF2 will be allowed to reset it's yaw to the estimate from the EKF-GSF yaw estimator. No resets will be allowed unless the use of the EKF-GSF yaw estimate is enabled via the EK2_GSF_USE parameter.
EK2_GSF_RST_MAX.name: Maximum number of resets to the EKF-GSF yaw estimate allowed

EK2_GSF_RST_MAX.desc: Sets the maximum number of times the EKF2 will be allowed to reset its yaw to the estimate from the EKF-GSF yaw estimator. No resets will be allowed unless the use of the EKF-GSF yaw estimate is enabled via the EK2_GSF_USE_MASK parameter.
EK2_GSF_RST_MAX.name: Maximum number of resets to the EKF-GSF yaw estimate allowed

EK2_GSF_RUN_MASK.desc: 1 byte bitmap of which EKF2 instances run an independant EKF-GSF yaw estimator to provide a backup yaw estimate that doesn't rely on magnetometer data. This estimator uses IMU, GPS and, if available, airspeed data. EKF-GSF yaw estimator data for the primary EKF2 instance will be logged as GSF0 and GSF1 messages. Use of the yaw estimate generated by this algorithm is controlled by the EK2_GSF_USE, EK2_GSF_DELAY and EK2_GSF_MAXCOUNT parameters. To run the EKF-GSF yaw estimator in ride-along and logging only, set EK2_GSF_USE to 0.
EK2_GSF_RUN_MASK.name: Bitmask of which EKF-GSF yaw estimators run

EK2_GSF_RUN_MASK.desc: A bitmask of which EKF2 instances run an independant EKF-GSF yaw estimator to provide a backup yaw estimate that doesn't rely on magnetometer data. This estimator uses IMU, GPS and, if available, airspeed data. EKF-GSF yaw estimator data for the primary EKF2 instance will be logged as GSF0 and GSF1 messages. Use of the yaw estimate generated by this algorithm is controlled by the EK2_GSF_USE_MASK and EK2_GSF_RST_MAX parameters. To run the EKF-GSF yaw estimator in ride-along and logging only, set EK2_GSF_USE_MASK to 0.
EK2_GSF_RUN_MASK.name: Bitmask of which EKF-GSF yaw estimators run

EK2_GSF_USE_MASK.desc: 1 byte bitmap of which EKF2 instances will use the output from the EKF-GSF yaw estimator that has been turned on by the EK2_GSF_RUN parameter. If the inertial navigation calculation stops following the GPS, then the vehicle code can request EKF2 to attempt to resolve the issue, either by performing a yaw reset if enabled by this parameter by switching to another EKF2 instance. Additionally the EKF2 will initiate a reset internally if navigation is lost for more than EK2_GSF_DELAY milli seconds.
EK2_GSF_USE_MASK.name: Bitmask of which EKF-GSF yaw estimators are used

EK2_GSF_USE_MASK.desc: 1 byte bitmap of which EKF2 instances will use the output from the EKF-GSF yaw estimator that has been turned on by the EK2_GSF_RUN_MASK parameter. If the inertial navigation calculation stops following the GPS, then the vehicle code can request EKF2 to attempt to resolve the issue, either by performing a yaw reset if enabled by this parameter by switching to another EKF2 instance.
EK2_GSF_USE_MASK.name: Bitmask of which EKF-GSF yaw estimators are used

EK2_GYRO_P_NSE.desc: This control disturbance noise controls the growth of estimated error due to gyro measurement errors excluding bias. Increasing it makes the flter trust the gyro measurements less and other measurements more.
EK2_GYRO_P_NSE.name: Rate gyro noise (rad/s)

EK2_HGT_DELAY.desc: This is the number of msec that the Height measurements lag behind the inertial measurements.
EK2_HGT_DELAY.name: Height measurement delay (msec)

EK2_HGT_I_GATE.desc: This sets the percentage number of standard deviations applied to the height measurement innovation consistency check. Decreasing it makes it more likely that good measurements will be rejected. Increasing it makes it more likely that bad measurements will be accepted.
EK2_HGT_I_GATE.name: Height measurement gate size

EK2_HRT_FILT.desc: Specifies the crossover frequency of the complementary filter used to calculate the output predictor height rate derivative.
EK2_HRT_FILT.name: Height rate filter crossover frequency

EK2_IMU_MASK.desc: 1 byte bitmap of IMUs to use in EKF2. A separate instance of EKF2 will be started for each IMU selected. Set to 1 to use the first IMU only (default), set to 2 to use the second IMU only, set to 3 to use the first and second IMU. Additional IMU's can be used up to a maximum of 6 if memory and processing resources permit. There may be insufficient memory and processing resources to run multiple instances. If this occurs EKF2 will fail to start.
EK2_IMU_MASK.name: Bitmask of active IMUs

EK2_LOG_MASK.desc: This sets the IMU mask of sensors to do full logging for
EK2_LOG_MASK.name: EKF sensor logging IMU mask

EK2_MAGB_P_NSE.desc: This state process noise controls the growth of body magnetic field state error estimates. Increasing it makes magnetometer bias error estimation faster and noisier.
EK2_MAGB_P_NSE.name: Body magnetic field process noise (gauss/s)

EK2_MAGE_P_NSE.desc: This state process noise controls the growth of earth magnetic field state error estimates. Increasing it makes earth magnetic field estimation faster and noisier.
EK2_MAGE_P_NSE.name: Earth magnetic field process noise (gauss/s)

EK2_MAG_CAL.desc: This determines when the filter will use the 3-axis magnetometer fusion model that estimates both earth and body fixed magnetic field states and when it will use a simpler magnetic heading fusion model that does not use magnetic field states. The 3-axis magnetometer fusion is only suitable for use when the external magnetic field environment is stable. EK2_MAG_CAL = 0 uses heading fusion on ground, 3-axis fusion in-flight, and is the default setting for Plane users. EK2_MAG_CAL = 1 uses 3-axis fusion only when manoeuvring. EK2_MAG_CAL = 2 uses heading fusion at all times, is recommended if the external magnetic field is varying and is the default for rovers. EK2_MAG_CAL = 3 uses heading fusion on the ground and 3-axis fusion after the first in-air field and yaw reset has completed, and is the default for copters. EK2_MAG_CAL = 4 uses 3-axis fusion at all times. NOTE : Use of simple heading magnetometer fusion makes vehicle compass calibration and alignment errors harder for the EKF to detect which reduces the sensitivity of the Copter EKF failsafe algorithm. NOTE: The fusion mode can be forced to 2 for specific EKF cores using the EK2_MAG_MASK parameter.
EK2_MAG_CAL.name: Magnetometer default fusion mode

EK2_MAG_CAL.desc: This determines when the filter will use the 3-axis magnetometer fusion model that estimates both earth and body fixed magnetic field states, when it will use a simpler magnetic heading fusion model that does not use magnetic field states and when it will use an alternative method of yaw determination to the magnetometer. The 3-axis magnetometer fusion is only suitable for use when the external magnetic field environment is stable. EK2_MAG_CAL = 0 uses heading fusion on ground, 3-axis fusion in-flight, and is the default setting for Plane users. EK2_MAG_CAL = 1 uses 3-axis fusion only when manoeuvring. EK2_MAG_CAL = 2 uses heading fusion at all times, is recommended if the external magnetic field is varying and is the default for rovers. EK2_MAG_CAL = 3 uses heading fusion on the ground and 3-axis fusion after the first in-air field and yaw reset has completed, and is the default for copters. EK2_MAG_CAL = 4 uses 3-axis fusion at all times. NOTE: The fusion mode can be forced to 2 for specific EKF cores using the EK2_MAG_MASK parameter. NOTE: limited operation without a magnetometer or any other yaw sensor is possible by setting all COMPASS_USE, COMPASS_USE2, COMPASS_USE3, etc parameters to 0 with COMPASS_ENABLE set to 1. If this is done, the EK2_GSF_RUN and EK2_GSF_USE masks must be set to the same as EK2_IMU_MASK.
EK2_MAG_CAL.name: Magnetometer default fusion mode

EK2_MAG_EF_LIM.desc: This limits the difference between the learned earth magnetic field and the earth field from the world magnetic model tables. A value of zero means to disable the use of the WMM tables.
EK2_MAG_EF_LIM.name: EarthField error limit

EK2_MAG_I_GATE.desc: This sets the percentage number of standard deviations applied to the magnetometer measurement innovation consistency check. Decreasing it makes it more likely that good measurements will be rejected. Increasing it makes it more likely that bad measurements will be accepted.
EK2_MAG_I_GATE.name: Magnetometer measurement gate size

EK2_MAG_MASK.desc: 1 byte bitmap of EKF cores that will disable magnetic field states and use simple magnetic heading fusion at all times. This parameter enables specified cores to be used as a backup for flight into an environment with high levels of external magnetic interference which may degrade the EKF attitude estimate when using 3-axis magnetometer fusion. NOTE : Use of a different magnetometer fusion algorithm on different cores makes unwanted EKF core switches due to magnetometer errors more likely.
EK2_MAG_MASK.name: Bitmask of active EKF cores that will always use heading fusion

EK2_MAG_M_NSE.desc: This is the RMS value of noise in magnetometer measurements. Increasing it reduces the weighting on these measurements.
EK2_MAG_M_NSE.name: Magnetometer measurement noise (Gauss)

EK2_MAX_FLOW.desc: This sets the magnitude maximum optical flow rate in rad/sec that will be accepted by the filter
EK2_MAX_FLOW.name: Maximum valid optical flow rate

EK2_NOAID_M_NSE.desc: This sets the amount of position variation that the EKF allows for when operating without external measurements (eg GPS or optical flow). Increasing this parameter makes the EKF attitude estimate less sensitive to vehicle manoeuvres but more sensitive to IMU errors.
EK2_NOAID_M_NSE.name: Non-GPS operation position uncertainty (m)

bits: Correct when using range finder height
EK2_OGN_HGT_MASK.desc: When a height sensor other than GPS is used as the primary height source by the EKF, the position of the zero height datum is defined by that sensor and its frame of reference. If a GPS height measurement is also available, then the height of the WGS-84 height datum used by the EKF can be corrected so that the height returned by the getLLH() function is compensated for primary height sensor drift and change in datum over time. The first two bit positions control when the height datum will be corrected. Correction is performed using a Bayes filter and only operates when GPS quality permits. The third bit position controls where the corrections to the GPS reference datum are applied. Corrections can be applied to the local vertical position or to the reported EKF origin height (default).
EK2_OGN_HGT_MASK.name: Bitmask control of EKF reference height correction

EK2_OPTIONS.desc: optional EKF2 behaviour. Disabling external navigation prevents use of external vision data in the EKF2 solution
EK2_OPTIONS.name: Optional EKF behaviour

EK2_POSNE_M_NSE.desc: This sets the GPS horizontal position or external navigation system position observation noise. Increasing it reduces the weighting of GPS horizontal position or external navigation system position measurements.
EK2_POSNE_M_NSE.name: GPS horizontal position measurement noise (m)

EK2_POSNE_M_NSE.desc: This sets the GPS horizontal position observation noise. Increasing it reduces the weighting of GPS horizontal position measurements.
EK2_POSNE_M_NSE.name: GPS horizontal position measurement noise (m)

EK2_POS_I_GATE.desc: This sets the percentage number of standard deviations applied to the GPS position measurement innovation consistency check. Decreasing it makes it more likely that good measurements will be rejected. Increasing it makes it more likely that bad measurements will be accepted.
EK2_POS_I_GATE.name: GPS position measurement gate size

EK2_RNG_I_GATE.desc: This sets the percentage number of standard deviations applied to the range finder innovation consistency check. Decreasing it makes it more likely that good measurements will be rejected. Increasing it makes it more likely that bad measurements will be accepted.
EK2_RNG_I_GATE.name: Range finder measurement gate size

EK2_RNG_M_NSE.desc: This is the RMS value of noise in the range finder measurement. Increasing it reduces the weighting on this measurement.
EK2_RNG_M_NSE.name: Range finder measurement noise (m)

EK2_RNG_USE_HGT.desc: Range finder can be used as the primary height source when below this percentage of its maximum range (see RNGFND_MAX_CM). Set to -1 when EK2_ALT_SOURCE is not set to range finder. This is not for terrain following.
EK2_RNG_USE_HGT.name: Range finder switch height percentage

EK2_RNG_USE_HGT.desc: Range finder can be used as the primary height source when below this percentage of its maximum range (see RNGFND_MAX_CM). This will not work unless Baro or GPS height is selected as the primary height source vis EK2_ALT_SOURCE = 0 or 2 respectively. This feature should not be used for terrain following as it is designed for vertical takeoff and landing with climb above the range finder use height before commencing the mission, and with horizontal position changes below that height being limited to a flat region around the takeoff and landing point.
EK2_RNG_USE_HGT.name: Range finder switch height percentage

EK2_RNG_USE_HGT.desc: Range finder can be used as the primary height source when below this percentage of its maximum range (see RNGFND*_MAX). This will not work unless Baro or GPS height is selected as the primary height source vis EK2_ALT_SOURCE = 0 or 2 respectively. This feature should not be used for terrain following as it is designed for vertical takeoff and landing with climb above the range finder use height before commencing the mission, and with horizontal position changes below that height being limited to a flat region around the takeoff and landing point.
EK2_RNG_USE_HGT.name: Range finder switch height percentage

EK2_RNG_USE_SPD.desc: The range finder will not be used as the primary height source when the horizontal ground speed is greater than this value.
EK2_RNG_USE_SPD.name: Range finder max ground speed

EK2_TAU_OUTPUT.desc: Sets the time constant of the output complementary filter/predictor in centi-seconds.
EK2_TAU_OUTPUT.name: Output complementary filter time constant (centi-sec)

EK2_TERR_GRAD.desc: Specifies the maximum gradient of the terrain below the vehicle assumed when it is fusing range finder or optical flow to estimate terrain height.
EK2_TERR_GRAD.name: Maximum terrain gradient

EK2_VELD_M_NSE.desc: This sets a lower limit on the speed accuracy reported by the GPS receiver that is used to set vertical velocity observation noise. If the model of receiver used does not provide a speed accurcy estimate, then the parameter value will be used. Increasing it reduces the weighting of the GPS vertical velocity measurements.
EK2_VELD_M_NSE.name: GPS vertical velocity measurement noise (m/s)

EK2_VELNE_M_NSE.desc: This sets a lower limit on the speed accuracy reported by the GPS receiver that is used to set horizontal velocity observation noise. If the model of receiver used does not provide a speed accurcy estimate, then the parameter value will be used. Increasing it reduces the weighting of the GPS horizontal velocity measurements.
EK2_VELNE_M_NSE.name: GPS horizontal velocity measurement noise (m/s)

EK2_VEL_I_GATE.desc: This sets the percentage number of standard deviations applied to the GPS velocity measurement innovation consistency check. Decreasing it makes it more likely that good measurements willbe rejected. Increasing it makes it more likely that bad measurements will be accepted.
EK2_VEL_I_GATE.name: GPS velocity innovation gate size

EK2_VEL_I_GATE.desc: This sets the percentage number of standard deviations applied to the GPS velocity measurement innovation consistency check. Decreasing it makes it more likely that good measurements will be rejected. Increasing it makes it more likely that bad measurements will be accepted.
EK2_VEL_I_GATE.name: GPS velocity innovation gate size

EK2_WIND_PSCALE.desc: This controls how much the process noise on the wind states is increased when gaining or losing altitude to take into account changes in wind speed and direction with altitude. Increasing this parameter increases how rapidly the wind states adapt when changing altitude, but does make wind velocity estimation noiser.
EK2_WIND_PSCALE.name: Height rate to wind process noise scaler

EK2_WIND_P_NSE.desc: This state process noise controls the growth of wind state error estimates. Increasing it makes wind estimation faster and noisier.
EK2_WIND_P_NSE.name: Wind velocity process noise (m/s^2)

EK2_YAW_I_GATE.desc: This sets the percentage number of standard deviations applied to the magnetometer yaw measurement innovation consistency check. Decreasing it makes it more likely that good measurements will be rejected. Increasing it makes it more likely that bad measurements will be accepted.
EK2_YAW_I_GATE.name: Yaw measurement gate size

EK2_YAW_M_NSE.desc: This is the RMS value of noise in yaw measurements from the magnetometer. Increasing it reduces the weighting on these measurements.
EK2_YAW_M_NSE.name: Yaw measurement noise (rad)

EK3_ABIAS_P_NSE.desc: This noise controls the growth of the vertical accelerometer delta velocity bias state error estimate. Increasing it makes accelerometer bias estimation faster and noisier.
EK3_ABIAS_P_NSE.name: Accelerometer bias stability (m/s^3)

EK3_ABIAS_P_NSE.desc: This noise controls the growth of the vertical accelerometer delta velocity bias state error estimate. Increasing it makes accelerometer bias estimation faster and noisier.
EK3_ABIAS_P_NSE.name: Accelerometer bias stability (m/s^3)

EK3_ACC_BIAS_LIM.desc: The accelerometer bias state will be limited to +- this value
EK3_ACC_BIAS_LIM.name: Accelerometer bias limit

EK3_ACC_P_NSE.desc: This control disturbance noise controls the growth of estimated error due to accelerometer measurement errors excluding bias. Increasing it makes the flter trust the accelerometer measurements less and other measurements more.
EK3_ACC_P_NSE.name: Accelerometer noise (m/s^2)

EK3_AFFINITY.desc: These options control the affinity between sensor instances and EKF cores
EK3_AFFINITY.name: EKF3 Sensor Affinity Options

EK3_ALT_M_NSE.desc: This is the RMS value of noise in the altitude measurement. Increasing it reduces the weighting of the baro measurement and will make the filter respond more slowly to baro measurement errors, but will make it more sensitive to GPS and accelerometer errors.
EK3_ALT_M_NSE.name: Altitude measurement noise (m)

EK3_ALT_M_NSE.desc: This is the RMS value of noise in the altitude measurement. Increasing it reduces the weighting of the baro measurement and will make the filter respond more slowly to baro measurement errors, but will make it more sensitive to GPS and accelerometer errors. A larger value for EK3_ALT_M_NSE may be required when operating with EK3_SRCx_POSZ = 0. This parameter also sets the noise for the 'synthetic' zero height measurement that is used when EK3_SRCx_POSZ = 0.
EK3_ALT_M_NSE.name: Altitude measurement noise (m)

EK3_ALT_M_NSE.desc: This is the RMS value of noise in the altitude measurement. Increasing it reduces the weighting of the baro measurement and will make the filter respond more slowly to baro measurement errors, but will make it more sensitive to GPS and accelerometer errors. A larger value for EK3_ALT_M_NSE may be required when operating with EK3_SRCx_POSZ = 0. This parameter also sets the noise for the 'synthetic' zero height measurement that is used when EK3_SRCx_POSZ = 0.
EK3_ALT_M_NSE.name: Altitude measurement noise (m)

EK3_ALT_SOURCE.desc: Primary height sensor used by the EKF. If the selected option cannot be used, baro is used. 1 uses the range finder and only with optical flow navigation (EK2_GPS_TYPE = 3), Do not use "1" for terrain following. NOTE: the EK3_RNG_USE_HGT parameter can be used to switch to range-finder when close to the ground.
EK3_ALT_SOURCE.name: Primary altitude sensor source

EK3_BCN_DELAY.desc: This is the number of msec that the range beacon measurements lag behind the inertial measurements.
EK3_BCN_DELAY.name: Range beacon measurement delay (msec)

EK3_BCN_I_GTE.desc: This sets the percentage number of standard deviations applied to the range beacon measurement innovation consistency check. Decreasing it makes it more likely that good measurements will be rejected. Increasing it makes it more likely that bad measurements will be accepted.
EK3_BCN_I_GTE.name: Range beacon measurement gate size

EK3_BCN_M_NSE.desc: This is the RMS value of noise in the range beacon measurement. Increasing it reduces the weighting on this measurement.
EK3_BCN_M_NSE.name: Range beacon measurement noise (m)

EK3_BETA_MASK.desc: 1 byte bitmap controlling use of sideslip angle fusion for estimation of non wind states during operation of 'fly forward' vehicle types such as fixed wing planes. By assuming that the angle of sideslip is small, the wind velocity state estimates are corrected whenever the EKF is not dead reckoning (e.g. has an independent velocity or position sensor such as GPS). This behaviour is on by default and cannot be disabled. When the EKF is dead reckoning, the wind states are used as a reference, enabling use of the small angle of sideslip assumption to correct non wind velocity states (eg attitude, velocity, position, etc) and improve navigation accuracy. This behaviour is on by default and cannot be disabled. The behaviour controlled by this parameter is the use of the small angle of sideslip assumption to correct non wind velocity states when the EKF is NOT dead reckoning. This is primarily of benefit to reduce the buildup of yaw angle errors during straight and level flight without a yaw sensor (e.g. magnetometer or dual antenna GPS yaw) provided aerobatic flight maneuvers with large sideslip angles are not performed. The 'always' option might be used where the yaw sensor is intentionally not fitted or disabled. The 'WhenNoYawSensor' option might be used if a yaw sensor is fitted, but protection against in-flight failure and continual rejection by the EKF is desired. For vehicles operated within visual range of the operator performing frequent turning maneuvers, setting this parameter is unnecessary.
EK3_BETA_MASK.name: Bitmask controlling sidelip angle fusion

EK3_CHECK_SCALE.desc: This scales the thresholds that are used to check GPS accuracy before it is used by the EKF. A value of 100 is the default. Values greater than 100 increase and values less than 100 reduce the maximum GPS error the EKF will accept. A value of 200 will double the allowable GPS error.
EK3_CHECK_SCALE.name: GPS accuracy check scaler (%)

EK3_DRAG_BCOEF_X.desc: Ratio of mass to drag coefficient measured along the X body axis. This parameter enables estimation of wind drift for vehicles with bluff bodies and without propulsion forces in the X and Y direction (eg multicopters). The drag produced by this effect scales with speed squared. Set to a postive value > 1.0 to enable. A starting value is the mass in Kg divided by the frontal area. The predicted drag from the rotors is specified separately by the EK3_MCOEF parameter.
EK3_DRAG_BCOEF_X.name: Ballistic coefficient for X axis drag

EK3_DRAG_BCOEF_X.desc: Ratio of mass to drag coefficient measured along the X body axis. This parameter enables estimation of wind drift for vehicles with bluff bodies and without propulsion forces in the X and Y direction (eg multicopters). The drag produced by this effect scales with speed squared. Set to a postive value > 1.0 to enable. A starting value is the mass in Kg divided by the frontal area. The predicted drag from the rotors is specified separately by the EK3_DRAG_MCOEF parameter.
EK3_DRAG_BCOEF_X.name: Ballistic coefficient for X axis drag

EK3_DRAG_BCOEF_X.desc: Ratio of mass to drag coefficient measured along the X body axis. This parameter enables estimation of wind drift for vehicles with bluff bodies and without propulsion forces in the X and Y direction (eg multicopters). The drag produced by this effect scales with speed squared. Set to a positive value > 1.0 to enable. A starting value is the mass in Kg divided by the frontal area. The predicted drag from the rotors is specified separately by the EK3_DRAG_MCOEF parameter.
EK3_DRAG_BCOEF_X.name: Ballistic coefficient for X axis drag

EK3_DRAG_BCOEF_Y.desc: Ratio of mass to drag coefficient measured along the Y body axis. This parameter enables estimation of wind drift for vehicles with bluff bodies and without propulsion forces in the X and Y direction (eg multicopters). The drag produced by this effect scales with speed squared. Set to a postive value > 1.0 to enable. A starting value is the mass in Kg divided by the side area. The predicted drag from the rotors is specified separately by the EK3_MCOEF parameter.
EK3_DRAG_BCOEF_Y.name: Ballistic coefficient for Y axis drag

EK3_DRAG_BCOEF_Y.desc: Ratio of mass to drag coefficient measured along the Y body axis. This parameter enables estimation of wind drift for vehicles with bluff bodies and without propulsion forces in the X and Y direction (eg multicopters). The drag produced by this effect scales with speed squared. Set to a postive value > 1.0 to enable. A starting value is the mass in Kg divided by the side area. The predicted drag from the rotors is specified separately by the EK3_DRAG_MCOEF parameter.
EK3_DRAG_BCOEF_Y.name: Ballistic coefficient for Y axis drag

EK3_DRAG_BCOEF_Y.desc: Ratio of mass to drag coefficient measured along the Y body axis. This parameter enables estimation of wind drift for vehicles with bluff bodies and without propulsion forces in the X and Y direction (eg multicopters). The drag produced by this effect scales with speed squared. Set to a positive value > 1.0 to enable. A starting value is the mass in Kg divided by the side area. The predicted drag from the rotors is specified separately by the EK3_DRAG_MCOEF parameter.
EK3_DRAG_BCOEF_Y.name: Ballistic coefficient for Y axis drag

EK3_DRAG_MCOEF.desc: This parameter is used to predict the drag produced by the rotors when flying a multi-copter, enabling estimation of wind drift. The drag produced by this effect scales with speed not speed squared and is produced because some of the air velocity normal to the rotors axis of rotation is lost when passing through the rotor disc which changes the momentum of the airflow causing drag. For unducted rotors the effect is roughly proportional to the area of the propeller blades when viewed side on and changes with different propellers. It is higher for ducted rotors. For example if flying at 15 m/s at sea level conditions produces a rotor induced drag acceleration of 1.5 m/s/s, then EK3_MCOEF would be set to 0.1 = (1.5/15.0). Set EK3_MCOEF to a postive value to enable wind estimation using this drag effect. To account for the drag produced by the body which scales with speed squared, see documentation for the EK3_BCOEF_X and EK3_BCOEF_Y parameters.
EK3_DRAG_MCOEF.name: Momentum coefficient for propeller drag

EK3_DRAG_MCOEF.desc: This parameter is used to predict the drag produced by the rotors when flying a multi-copter, enabling estimation of wind drift. The drag produced by this effect scales with speed not speed squared and is produced because some of the air velocity normal to the rotors axis of rotation is lost when passing through the rotor disc which changes the momentum of the airflow causing drag. For unducted rotors the effect is roughly proportional to the area of the propeller blades when viewed side on and changes with different propellers. It is higher for ducted rotors. For example if flying at 15 m/s at sea level conditions produces a rotor induced drag acceleration of 1.5 m/s/s, then EK3_DRAG_MCOEF would be set to 0.1 = (1.5/15.0). Set EK3_MCOEF to a postive value to enable wind estimation using this drag effect. To account for the drag produced by the body which scales with speed squared, see documentation for the EK3_DRAG_BCOEF_X and EK3_DRAG_BCOEF_Y parameters.
EK3_DRAG_MCOEF.name: Momentum coefficient for propeller drag

EK3_DRAG_MCOEF.desc: This parameter is used to predict the drag produced by the rotors when flying a multi-copter, enabling estimation of wind drift. The drag produced by this effect scales with speed not speed squared and is produced because some of the air velocity normal to the rotors axis of rotation is lost when passing through the rotor disc which changes the momentum of the airflow causing drag. For unducted rotors the effect is roughly proportional to the area of the propeller blades when viewed side on and changes with different propellers. It is higher for ducted rotors. For example if flying at 15 m/s at sea level conditions produces a rotor induced drag acceleration of 1.5 m/s/s, then EK3_DRAG_MCOEF would be set to 0.1 = (1.5/15.0). Set EK3_MCOEF to a positive value to enable wind estimation using this drag effect. To account for the drag produced by the body which scales with speed squared, see documentation for the EK3_DRAG_BCOEF_X and EK3_DRAG_BCOEF_Y parameters.
EK3_DRAG_MCOEF.name: Momentum coefficient for propeller drag

EK3_DRAG_M_NSE.desc: This sets the amount of noise used when fusing X and Y acceleration as an observation that enables esitmation of wind velocity for multi-rotor vehicles. This feature is enabled by the EK3_BCOEF_X and EK3_BCOEF_Y parameters
EK3_DRAG_M_NSE.name: Observation noise for drag acceleration

EK3_DRAG_M_NSE.desc: This sets the amount of noise used when fusing X and Y acceleration as an observation that enables esitmation of wind velocity for multi-rotor vehicles. This feature is enabled by the EK3_DRAG_BCOEF_X and EK3_DRAG_BCOEF_Y parameters
EK3_DRAG_M_NSE.name: Observation noise for drag acceleration

EK3_DRAG_M_NSE.desc: This sets the amount of noise used when fusing X and Y acceleration as an observation that enables estimation of wind velocity for multi-rotor vehicles. This feature is enabled by the EK3_DRAG_BCOEF_X and EK3_DRAG_BCOEF_Y parameters
EK3_DRAG_M_NSE.name: Observation noise for drag acceleration

EK3_EAS_I_GATE.desc: This sets the percentage number of standard deviations applied to the airspeed measurement innovation consistency check. Decreasing it makes it more likely that good measurements will be rejected. Increasing it makes it more likely that bad measurements will be accepted.
EK3_EAS_I_GATE.name: Airspeed measurement gate size

EK3_EAS_M_NSE.desc: This is the RMS value of noise in equivalent airspeed measurements used by planes. Increasing it reduces the weighting of airspeed measurements and will make wind speed estimates less noisy and slower to converge. Increasing also increases navigation errors when dead-reckoning without GPS measurements.
EK3_EAS_M_NSE.name: Equivalent airspeed measurement noise (m/s)

EK3_ENABLE.desc: This enables EKF3. Enabling EKF3 only makes the maths run, it does not mean it will be used for flight control. To use it for flight control set AHRS_EKF_TYPE=3. A reboot or restart will need to be performed after changing the value of EK3_ENABLE for it to take effect.
EK3_ENABLE.name: Enable EKF3

EK3_ERR_THRESH.desc: lanes have to be consistently better than the primary by at least this threshold to reduce their overall relativeCoreError, lowering this makes lane switching more sensitive to smaller error differences
EK3_ERR_THRESH.name: EKF3 Lane Relative Error Sensitivity Threshold

EK3_FLOW_DELAY.desc: This is the number of msec that the optical flow measurements lag behind the inertial measurements. It is the time from the end of the optical flow averaging period and does not include the time delay due to the 100msec of averaging within the flow sensor.
EK3_FLOW_DELAY.name: Optical Flow measurement delay (msec)

EK3_FLOW_GAIN_H.desc: Height below which the navigation velocity gain is left at full scale while navigating on optical flow. Above it the gain falls as this value divided by the height above ground, to allow for flow velocity noise that grows with height. Larger values keep position hold more responsive at height, at more risk of a flow-driven oscillation. Values below 1 are treated as 1. Takes effect immediately.
EK3_FLOW_GAIN_H.name: Optical flow nav gain full-scale height

EK3_FLOW_I_GATE.desc: This sets the percentage number of standard deviations applied to the optical flow innovation consistency check. Decreasing it makes it more likely that good measurements will be rejected. Increasing it makes it more likely that bad measurements will be accepted.
EK3_FLOW_I_GATE.name: Optical Flow measurement gate size

EK3_FLOW_MAX.desc: The maximum optical flow rate in rad/sec that will be accepted by the filter. Flow rates above this value will not be fused.
EK3_FLOW_MAX.name: Optical flow rate maximum

EK3_FLOW_M_NSE.desc: This is the RMS value of noise and errors in optical flow measurements. Increasing it reduces the weighting on these measurements.
EK3_FLOW_M_NSE.name: Optical flow measurement noise (rad/s)

EK3_FLOW_USE.desc: Controls if the optical flow data is fused into the 24-state navigation estimator OR the 1-state terrain height estimator.
EK3_FLOW_USE.name: Optical flow use bitmask

EK3_GBIAS_P_NSE.desc: This state process noise controls growth of the gyro delta angle bias state error estimate. Increasing it makes rate gyro bias estimation faster and noisier.
EK3_GBIAS_P_NSE.name: Rate gyro bias stability (rad/s/s)

EK3_GLITCH_RAD.desc: This controls the maximum radial uncertainty in position between the value predicted by the filter and the value measured by the GPS before the filter position and velocity states are reset to the GPS. Making this value larger allows the filter to ignore larger GPS glitches but also means that non-GPS errors such as IMU and compass can create a larger error in position before the filter is forced back to the GPS position.
EK3_GLITCH_RAD.name: GPS glitch radius gate size (m)

EK3_GLITCH_RAD.desc: This controls the maximum radial uncertainty in position between the value predicted by the filter and the value measured by the GPS before the filter position and velocity states are reset to the GPS. Making this value larger allows the filter to ignore larger GPS glitches but also means that non-GPS errors such as IMU and compass can create a larger error in position before the filter is forced back to the GPS position. If EK3_GLITCH_RAD set to 0 the GPS innovations will be clipped instead of rejected if they exceed the gate size set by EK3_VEL_I_GATE and EK3_POS_I_GATE which can be useful if poor quality sensor data is causing GPS rejection and loss of navigation but does make the EKF more susceptible to GPS glitches. If setting EK3_GLITCH_RAD to 0 it is recommended to reduce EK3_VEL_I_GATE and EK3_POS_I_GATE to 300.
EK3_GLITCH_RAD.name: GPS glitch radius gate size (m)

EK3_GND_EFF_DZ.desc: This parameter sets the size of the dead zone that is applied to negative baro height spikes that can occur when takeing off or landing when a vehicle with lift rotors is operating in ground effect ground effect. Set to about 0.5m less than the amount of negative offset in baro height that occurs just prior to takeoff when lift motors are spooling up. Set to 0 if no ground effect is present.
EK3_GND_EFF_DZ.name: Baro height ground effect dead zone

EK3_GND_EFF_DZ.desc: This parameter sets the size of the dead zone that is applied to negative baro height spikes that can occur when taking off or landing when a vehicle with lift rotors is operating in ground effect ground effect. Set to about 0.5m less than the amount of negative offset in baro height that occurs just prior to takeoff when lift motors are spooling up. Set to 0 if no ground effect is present.
EK3_GND_EFF_DZ.name: Baro height ground effect dead zone

EK3_GPS_CHECK.desc: This is a 1 byte bitmap controlling which GPS preflight checks are performed. Set to 0 to bypass all checks. Set to 255 perform all checks. Set to 3 to check just the number of satellites and HDoP. Set to 31 for the most rigorous checks that will still allow checks to pass when the copter is moving, eg launch from a boat.
EK3_GPS_CHECK.name: GPS preflight check

EK3_GPS_TYPE.desc: This controls use of GPS measurements : 0 = use 3D velocity & 2D position, 1 = use 2D velocity and 2D position, 2 = use 2D position, 3 = Inhibit GPS use - this can be useful when flying with an optical flow sensor in an environment where GPS quality is poor and subject to large multipath errors.
EK3_GPS_TYPE.name: GPS mode control

EK3_GPS_VACC_MAX.desc: Vertical accuracy threshold for GPS as the altitude source. The GPS will not be used as an altitude source if the reported vertical accuracy of the GPS is larger than this threshold, falling back to baro instead. Set to zero to deactivate the threshold check.
EK3_GPS_VACC_MAX.name: GPS vertical accuracy threshold

EK3_GSF_RST_MAX.desc: Sets the maximum number of times the EKF3 will be allowed to reset it's yaw to the estimate from the EKF-GSF yaw estimator. No resets will be allowed unless the use of the EKF-GSF yaw estimate is enabled via the EK3_GSF_USE parameter.
EK3_GSF_RST_MAX.name: Maximum number of resets to the EKF-GSF yaw estimate allowed

EK3_GSF_RST_MAX.desc: Sets the maximum number of times the EKF3 will be allowed to reset its yaw to the estimate from the EKF-GSF yaw estimator. No resets will be allowed unless the use of the EKF-GSF yaw estimate is enabled via the EK3_GSF_USE_MASK parameter.
EK3_GSF_RST_MAX.name: Maximum number of resets to the EKF-GSF yaw estimate allowed

EK3_GSF_RUN_MASK.desc: 1 byte bitmap of which EKF3 instances run an independant EKF-GSF yaw estimator to provide a backup yaw estimate that doesn't rely on magnetometer data. This estimator uses IMU, GPS and, if available, airspeed data. EKF-GSF yaw estimator data for the primary EKF3 instance will be logged as GSF0 and GSF1 messages. Use of the yaw estimate generated by this algorithm is controlled by the EK3_GSF_USE, EK3_GSF_DELAY and EK3_GSF_MAXCOUNT parameters. To run the EKF-GSF yaw estimator in ride-along and logging only, set EK3_GSF_USE to 0.
EK3_GSF_RUN_MASK.name: Bitmask of which EKF-GSF yaw estimators run

EK3_GSF_RUN_MASK.desc: 1 byte bitmap of which EKF3 instances run an independant EKF-GSF yaw estimator to provide a backup yaw estimate that doesn't rely on magnetometer data. This estimator uses IMU, GPS and, if available, airspeed data. EKF-GSF yaw estimator data for the primary EKF3 instance will be logged as GSF0 and GSF1 messages. Use of the yaw estimate generated by this algorithm is controlled by the EK3_GSF_USE_MASK and EK3_GSF_RST_MAX parameters. To run the EKF-GSF yaw estimator in ride-along and logging only, set EK3_GSF_USE to 0.
EK3_GSF_RUN_MASK.name: Bitmask of which EKF-GSF yaw estimators run

EK3_GSF_RUN_MASK.desc: 1 byte bitmap of which EKF3 instances run an independent EKF-GSF yaw estimator to provide a backup yaw estimate that doesn't rely on magnetometer data. This estimator uses IMU, GPS and, if available, airspeed data. EKF-GSF yaw estimator data for the primary EKF3 instance will be logged as GSF0 and GSF1 messages. Use of the yaw estimate generated by this algorithm is controlled by the EK3_GSF_USE_MASK and EK3_GSF_RST_MAX parameters. To run the EKF-GSF yaw estimator in ride-along and logging only, set EK3_GSF_USE to 0.
EK3_GSF_RUN_MASK.name: Bitmask of which EKF-GSF yaw estimators run

EK3_GSF_USE_MASK.desc: 1 byte bitmap of which EKF3 instances will use the output from the EKF-GSF yaw estimator that has been turned on by the EK3_GSF_RUN parameter. If the inertial navigation calculation stops following the GPS, then the vehicle code can request EKF3 to attempt to resolve the issue, either by performing a yaw reset if enabled by this parameter by switching to another EKF3 instance. Additionally the EKF3 will initiate a reset internally if navigation is lost for more than EK3_GSF_DELAY milli seconds.
EK3_GSF_USE_MASK.name: Bitmask of which EKF-GSF yaw estimators are used

EK3_GSF_USE_MASK.desc: A bitmask of which EKF3 instances will use the output from the EKF-GSF yaw estimator that has been turned on by the EK3_GSF_RUN_MASK parameter. If the inertial navigation calculation stops following the GPS, then the vehicle code can request EKF3 to attempt to resolve the issue, either by performing a yaw reset if enabled by this parameter by switching to another EKF3 instance.
EK3_GSF_USE_MASK.name: Bitmask of which EKF-GSF yaw estimators are used

EK3_GYRO_P_NSE.desc: This control disturbance noise controls the growth of estimated error due to gyro measurement errors excluding bias. Increasing it makes the flter trust the gyro measurements less and other measurements more.
EK3_GYRO_P_NSE.name: Rate gyro noise (rad/s)

EK3_HGT_DELAY.desc: This is the number of msec that the Height measurements lag behind the inertial measurements.
EK3_HGT_DELAY.name: Height measurement delay (msec)

EK3_HGT_I_GATE.desc: This sets the percentage number of standard deviations applied to the height measurement innovation consistency check. Decreasing it makes it more likely that good measurements will be rejected. Increasing it makes it more likely that bad measurements will be accepted.
EK3_HGT_I_GATE.name: Height measurement gate size

EK3_HGT_I_GATE.desc: This sets the percentage number of standard deviations applied to the height measurement innovation consistency check. Decreasing it makes it more likely that good measurements will be rejected. Increasing it makes it more likely that bad measurements will be accepted. If EK3_GLITCH_RAD set to 0 the vertical position innovations will be clipped instead of rejected if they exceed the gate size and a smaller value of EK3_HGT_I_GATE not exceeding 300 is recommended to limit the effect of height sensor transient errors.
EK3_HGT_I_GATE.name: Height measurement gate size

EK3_HRT_FILT.desc: Specifies the crossover frequency of the complementary filter used to calculate the output predictor height rate derivative.
EK3_HRT_FILT.name: Height rate filter crossover frequency

EK3_IMU_MASK.desc: 1 byte bitmap of IMUs to use in EKF3. A separate instance of EKF3 will be started for each IMU selected. Set to 1 to use the first IMU only (default), set to 2 to use the second IMU only, set to 3 to use the first and second IMU. Additional IMU's can be used up to a maximum of 6 if memory and processing resources permit. There may be insufficient memory and processing resources to run multiple instances. If this occurs EKF3 will fail to start.
EK3_IMU_MASK.name: Bitmask of active IMUs

EK3_LOG_LEVEL.desc: Determines how verbose the EKF3 streaming logging is. A value of 0 provides full logging(default), a value of 1 only XKF4 scaled innovations are logged, a value of 2 both XKF4 and GSF are logged, and a value of 3 disables all streaming logging of EKF3.
EK3_LOG_LEVEL.name: Logging Level

EK3_LOG_MASK.desc: This sets the IMU mask of sensors to do full logging for
EK3_LOG_MASK.name: EKF sensor logging IMU mask

EK3_MAGB_P_NSE.desc: This state process noise controls the growth of body magnetic field state error estimates. Increasing it makes magnetometer bias error estimation faster and noisier.
EK3_MAGB_P_NSE.name: Body magnetic field process noise (gauss/s)

EK3_MAGE_P_NSE.desc: This state process noise controls the growth of earth magnetic field state error estimates. Increasing it makes earth magnetic field estimation faster and noisier.
EK3_MAGE_P_NSE.name: Earth magnetic field process noise (gauss/s)

EK3_MAG_CAL.desc: This determines when the filter will use the 3-axis magnetometer fusion model that estimates both earth and body fixed magnetic field states and when it will use a simpler magnetic heading fusion model that does not use magnetic field states. The 3-axis magnetometer fusion is only suitable for use when the external magnetic field environment is stable. EK3_MAG_CAL = 0 uses heading fusion on ground, 3-axis fusion in-flight, and is the default setting for Plane users. EK3_MAG_CAL = 1 uses 3-axis fusion only when manoeuvring. EK3_MAG_CAL = 2 uses heading fusion at all times, is recommended if the external magnetic field is varying and is the default for rovers. EK3_MAG_CAL = 3 uses heading fusion on the ground and 3-axis fusion after the first in-air field and yaw reset has completed, and is the default for copters. EK3_MAG_CAL = 4 uses 3-axis fusion at all times. EK3_MAG_CAL = 5 uses an external yaw sensor with simple heading fusion. NOTE : Use of simple heading magnetometer fusion makes vehicle compass calibration and alignment errors harder for the EKF to detect which reduces the sensitivity of the Copter EKF failsafe algorithm. NOTE: The fusion mode can be forced to 2 for specific EKF cores using the EK3_MAG_MASK parameter.
EK3_MAG_CAL.name: Magnetometer default fusion mode

EK3_MAG_CAL.desc: This determines when the filter will use the 3-axis magnetometer fusion model that estimates both earth and body fixed magnetic field states and when it will use a simpler magnetic heading fusion model that does not use magnetic field states. The 3-axis magnetometer fusion is only suitable for use when the external magnetic field environment is stable. EK3_MAG_CAL = 0 uses heading fusion on ground, 3-axis fusion in-flight, and is the default setting for Plane users. EK3_MAG_CAL = 1 uses 3-axis fusion only when manoeuvring. EK3_MAG_CAL = 2 uses heading fusion at all times, is recommended if the external magnetic field is varying and is the default for rovers. EK3_MAG_CAL = 3 uses heading fusion on the ground and 3-axis fusion after the first in-air field and yaw reset has completed, and is the default for copters. EK3_MAG_CAL = 4 uses 3-axis fusion at all times. EK3_MAG_CAL = 5 uses an external yaw sensor with simple heading fusion. NOTE : Use of simple heading magnetometer fusion makes vehicle compass calibration and alignment errors harder for the EKF to detect which reduces the sensitivity of the Copter EKF failsafe algorithm. NOTE: The fusion mode can be forced to 2 for specific EKF cores using the EK3_MAG_MASK parameter. EK3_MAG_CAL = 6 uses an external yaw sensor with fallback to compass when the external sensor is not available if we are flying. NOTE: The fusion mode can be forced to 2 for specific EKF cores using the EK3_MAG_MASK parameter. NOTE: limited operation without a magnetometer or any other yaw sensor is possible by setting all COMPASS_USE, COMPASS_USE2, COMPASS_USE3, etc parameters to 0 and setting COMPASS_ENABLE to 0. If this is done, the EK3_GSF_RUN and EK3_GSF_USE masks must be set to the same as EK3_IMU_MASK. A yaw angle derived from IMU and GPS velocity data using a Gaussian Sum Filter (GSF) will then be used to align the yaw when flight commences and there is sufficient movement.
EK3_MAG_CAL.name: Magnetometer default fusion mode
values: Use external yaw sensor (Deprecated in 4.1+ see EK3_SRCn_YAW)
External yaw sensor with compass fallback (Deprecated in 4.1+ see EK3_SRCn_YAW)

EK3_MAG_CAL.desc: This determines when the filter will use the 3-axis magnetometer fusion model that estimates both earth and body fixed magnetic field states and when it will use a simpler magnetic heading fusion model that does not use magnetic field states. The 3-axis magnetometer fusion is only suitable for use when the external magnetic field environment is stable. EK3_MAG_CAL = 0 uses heading fusion on ground, 3-axis fusion in-flight, and is the default setting for Plane users. EK3_MAG_CAL = 1 uses 3-axis fusion only when manoeuvring. EK3_MAG_CAL = 2 uses heading fusion at all times, is recommended if the external magnetic field is varying and is the default for rovers. EK3_MAG_CAL = 3 uses heading fusion on the ground and 3-axis fusion after the first in-air field and yaw reset has completed, and is the default for copters. EK3_MAG_CAL = 4 uses 3-axis fusion at all times. EK3_MAG_CAL = 7 uses 3-axis fusion on the ground and after the first in-air field and yaw reset has completed. This allows the magnetic field to be learned on the ground before takeoff (useful when swapping batteries with different magnetic signatures) while inhibiting learning during the initial climb when motor magnetic interference is strongest. While disarmed and stationary the yaw is additionally anchored to the measured magnetic heading, since a stationary vehicle gives the 3-axis fusion no way to separate a yaw error from the body field states. A body field component perpendicular to the horizontal earth field is not separable from yaw by a heading measurement, so it appears as a heading offset rather than being learned. NOTE : Use of simple heading magnetometer fusion makes vehicle compass calibration and alignment errors harder for the EKF to detect which reduces the sensitivity of the Copter EKF failsafe algorithm. NOTE: The fusion mode can be forced to 2 for specific EKF cores using the EK3_MAG_MASK parameter. NOTE: limited operation without a magnetometer or any other yaw sensor is possible by setting all COMPASS_USE, COMPASS_USE2, COMPASS_USE3, etc parameters to 0 and setting COMPASS_ENABLE to 0. If this is done, the EK3_GSF_RUN and EK3_GSF_USE masks must be set to the same as EK3_IMU_MASK. A yaw angle derived from IMU and GPS velocity data using a Gaussian Sum Filter (GSF) will then be used to align the yaw when flight commences and there is sufficient movement.
EK3_MAG_CAL.name: Magnetometer default fusion mode
values: Use external yaw sensor (Deprecated in 4.1+ see EK3_SRCn_YAW)
External yaw sensor with compass fallback (Deprecated in 4.1+ see EK3_SRCn_YAW)

EK3_MAG_EF_LIM.desc: This limits the difference between the learned earth magnetic field and the earth field from the world magnetic model tables. A value of zero means to disable the use of the WMM tables.
EK3_MAG_EF_LIM.name: EarthField error limit

EK3_MAG_I_GATE.desc: This sets the percentage number of standard deviations applied to the magnetometer measurement innovation consistency check. Decreasing it makes it more likely that good measurements will be rejected. Increasing it makes it more likely that bad measurements will be accepted.
EK3_MAG_I_GATE.name: Magnetometer measurement gate size

EK3_MAG_MASK.desc: 1 byte bitmap of EKF cores that will disable magnetic field states and use simple magnetic heading fusion at all times. This parameter enables specified cores to be used as a backup for flight into an environment with high levels of external magnetic interference which may degrade the EKF attitude estimate when using 3-axis magnetometer fusion. NOTE : Use of a different magnetometer fusion algorithm on different cores makes unwanted EKF core switches due to magnetometer errors more likely.
EK3_MAG_MASK.name: Bitmask of active EKF cores that will always use heading fusion

EK3_MAG_M_NSE.desc: This is the RMS value of noise in magnetometer measurements. Increasing it reduces the weighting on these measurements.
EK3_MAG_M_NSE.name: Magnetometer measurement noise (Gauss)

EK3_MAX_FLOW.desc: This sets the magnitude maximum optical flow rate in rad/sec that will be accepted by the filter
EK3_MAX_FLOW.name: Maximum valid optical flow rate

EK3_NOAID_M_NSE.desc: This sets the amount of position variation that the EKF allows for when operating without external measurements (eg GPS or optical flow). Increasing this parameter makes the EKF attitude estimate less sensitive to vehicle manoeuvres but more sensitive to IMU errors.
EK3_NOAID_M_NSE.name: Non-GPS operation position uncertainty (m)

EK3_OGNM_TEST_SF.desc: This parameter is adjust the sensitivity of the on ground not moving test which is used to assist with learning the yaw gyro bias and stopping yaw drift before flight when operating without a yaw sensor. Bigger values allow the detection of a not moving condition with noiser IMU data. Check the XKFM data logged when the vehicle is on ground not moving and adjust the value of OGNM_TEST_SF to be slightly higher than the maximum value of the XKFM.ADR, XKFM.ALR, XKFM.GDR and XKFM.GLR test levels.
EK3_OGNM_TEST_SF.name: On ground not moving test scale factor

bits: Correct when using range finder height
EK3_OGN_HGT_MASK.desc: When a height sensor other than GPS is used as the primary height source by the EKF, the position of the zero height datum is defined by that sensor and its frame of reference. If a GPS height measurement is also available, then the height of the WGS-84 height datum used by the EKF can be corrected so that the height returned by the getLLH() function is compensated for primary height sensor drift and change in datum over time. The first two bit positions control when the height datum will be corrected. Correction is performed using a Bayes filter and only operates when GPS quality permits. The third bit position controls where the corrections to the GPS reference datum are applied. Corrections can be applied to the local vertical position or to the reported EKF origin height (default).
EK3_OGN_HGT_MASK.name: Bitmask control of EKF reference height correction

EK3_OPTIONS.desc: This controls optional EKF behaviour. Setting JammingExpected will change the EKF nehaviour such that if dead reckoning navigation is possible it will require the preflight alignment GPS quality checks controlled by EK3_GPS_CHECK and EK3_CHECK_SCALE to pass before resuming GPS use if GPS lock is lost for more than 2 seconds to prevent bad
EK3_OPTIONS.name: Optional EKF behaviour

EK3_OPTIONS.desc: EKF optional behaviour. Bit 0 (JammingExpected): Setting JammingExpected will change the EKF behaviour such that if dead reckoning navigation is possible it will require the preflight alignment GPS quality checks controlled by EK3_GPS_CHECK and EK3_CHECK_SCALE to pass before resuming GPS use if GPS lock is lost for more than 2 seconds to prevent bad position estimate. Bit 1 (Manual lane switching): DANGEROUS – If enabled, this disables automatic lane switching. If the active lane becomes unhealthy, no automatic switching will occur. Users must manually set EK3_PRIMARY to change lanes. No health checks will be performed on the selected lane. Use with extreme caution. Bit 2 (Optflow may use terrain alt): Terrain SRTM data will be used if the vehicle climbs above the rangefinder's range allowing optical flow to be used at higher altitudes.
EK3_OPTIONS.name: Optional EKF behaviour

EK3_OPTIONS.desc: EKF optional behaviour. Bit 0 (JammingExpected): Setting JammingExpected will change the EKF behaviour such that if dead reckoning navigation is possible it will require the preflight alignment GPS quality checks controlled by EK3_GPS_CHECK and EK3_CHECK_SCALE to pass before resuming GPS use if GPS lock is lost for more than 2 seconds to prevent bad position estimate. Bit 1 (Manual lane switching): DANGEROUS – If enabled, this disables automatic lane switching. If the active lane becomes unhealthy, no automatic switching will occur. Users must manually set EK3_PRIMARY to change lanes. No health checks will be performed on the selected lane. Use with extreme caution. Bit 2 (Optflow may use terrain alt): Terrain SRTM data will be used if the vehicle climbs above the rangefinder's range allowing optical flow to be used at higher altitudes. Bit 3 (AGL KF for optflow scaling): Use a 2-state IMU-aided AGL Kalman filter (height + vertical velocity, fused with rangefinder) to compute the height-above-ground used for optical flow velocity scaling, instead of terrainState-pd. This decouples optical flow scaling from errors in the main filter's vertical position state.
EK3_OPTIONS.name: Optional EKF behaviour

EK3_POSNE_M_NSE.desc: This sets the GPS horizontal position observation noise. Increasing it reduces the weighting of GPS horizontal position measurements.
EK3_POSNE_M_NSE.name: GPS horizontal position measurement noise (m)

EK3_POS_I_GATE.desc: This sets the percentage number of standard deviations applied to the GPS position measurement innovation consistency check. Decreasing it makes it more likely that good measurements will be rejected. Increasing it makes it more likely that bad measurements will be accepted.
EK3_POS_I_GATE.name: GPS position measurement gate size

EK3_POS_I_GATE.desc: This sets the percentage number of standard deviations applied to the GPS position measurement innovation consistency check. Decreasing it makes it more likely that good measurements will be rejected. Increasing it makes it more likely that bad measurements will be accepted. If EK3_GLITCH_RAD has been set to 0 the horizontal position innovations will be clipped instead of rejected if they exceed the gate size so a smaller value of EK3_POS_I_GATE not exceeding 300 is recommended to limit the effect of GPS transient errors.
EK3_POS_I_GATE.name: GPS position measurement gate size

EK3_PRIMARY.desc: The core number (index in IMU mask) that will be used as the primary EKF core on startup. While disarmed the EKF will force the use of this core. A value of 0 corresponds to the first IMU in EK3_IMU_MASK.
EK3_PRIMARY.name: Primary core number

EK3_RNG_I_GATE.desc: This sets the percentage number of standard deviations applied to the range finder innovation consistency check. Decreasing it makes it more likely that good measurements will be rejected. Increasing it makes it more likely that bad measurements will be accepted.
EK3_RNG_I_GATE.name: Range finder measurement gate size

EK3_RNG_M_NSE.desc: This is the RMS value of noise in the range finder measurement. Increasing it reduces the weighting on this measurement.
EK3_RNG_M_NSE.name: Range finder measurement noise (m)

EK3_RNG_USE_HGT.desc: Range finder can be used as the primary height source when below this percentage of its maximum range (see RNGFND_MAX_CM). Set to -1 when EK3_ALT_SOURCE is not set to range finder. This is not for terrain following.
EK3_RNG_USE_HGT.name: Range finder switch height percentage

EK3_RNG_USE_HGT.desc: Range finder can be used as the primary height source when below this percentage of its maximum range (see RNGFNDx_MAX_CM) and the primary height source is Baro or GPS (see EK3_SRCx_POSZ). This feature should not be used for terrain following as it is designed for vertical takeoff and landing with climb above the range finder use height before commencing the mission, and with horizontal position changes below that height being limited to a flat region around the takeoff and landing point.
EK3_RNG_USE_HGT.name: Range finder switch height percentage

EK3_RNG_USE_HGT.desc: Range finder can be used as the primary height source when below this percentage of its maximum range (see RNGFNDx_MAX) and the primary height source is Baro or GPS (see EK3_SRCx_POSZ). This feature should not be used for terrain following as it is designed for vertical takeoff and landing with climb above the range finder use height before commencing the mission, and with horizontal position changes below that height being limited to a flat region around the takeoff and landing point.
EK3_RNG_USE_HGT.name: Range finder switch height percentage

EK3_RNG_USE_SPD.desc: The range finder will not be used as the primary height source when the horizontal ground speed is greater than this value.
EK3_RNG_USE_SPD.name: Range finder max ground speed

EK3_SRC_OPTIONS.desc: EKF Source Options. Bit 0: Fuse all velocity sources present in EK3_SRCx_VEL_. Bit 1: Align external navigation position when using optical flow. Bit 3: Use SRC per core. By default, EKF source selection is controlled via the EK3_SRC parameters, allowing only one source to be active at a time across all cores (switchable via MAVLink, Lua, or RC). Enabling this bit maps EKF core 1 to SRC1, core 2 to SRC2, etc., allowing each core to run independently with a dedicated source.
EK3_SRC_OPTIONS.name: EKF Source Options

EK3_TAU_OUTPUT.desc: Sets the time constant of the output complementary filter/predictor in centi-seconds.
EK3_TAU_OUTPUT.name: Output complementary filter time constant (centi-sec)

EK3_TERR_GRAD.desc: Specifies the maximum gradient of the terrain below the vehicle when it is using range finder as a height reference
EK3_TERR_GRAD.name: Maximum terrain gradient

EK3_VELD_M_NSE.desc: This sets a lower limit on the speed accuracy reported by the GPS receiver that is used to set vertical velocity observation noise. If the model of receiver used does not provide a speed accurcy estimate, then the parameter value will be used. Increasing it reduces the weighting of the GPS vertical velocity measurements.
EK3_VELD_M_NSE.name: GPS vertical velocity measurement noise (m/s)

EK3_VELNE_M_NSE.desc: This sets a lower limit on the speed accuracy reported by the GPS receiver that is used to set horizontal velocity observation noise. If the model of receiver used does not provide a speed accurcy estimate, then the parameter value will be used. Increasing it reduces the weighting of the GPS horizontal velocity measurements.
EK3_VELNE_M_NSE.name: GPS horizontal velocity measurement noise (m/s)

EK3_VEL_I_GATE.desc: This sets the percentage number of standard deviations applied to the GPS velocity measurement innovation consistency check. Decreasing it makes it more likely that good measurements willbe rejected. Increasing it makes it more likely that bad measurements will be accepted.
EK3_VEL_I_GATE.name: GPS velocity innovation gate size

EK3_VEL_I_GATE.desc: This sets the percentage number of standard deviations applied to the GPS velocity measurement innovation consistency check. Decreasing it makes it more likely that good measurements will be rejected. Increasing it makes it more likely that bad measurements will be accepted.
EK3_VEL_I_GATE.name: GPS velocity innovation gate size

EK3_VEL_I_GATE.desc: This sets the percentage number of standard deviations applied to the GPS velocity measurement innovation consistency check. Decreasing it makes it more likely that good measurements will be rejected. Increasing it makes it more likely that bad measurements will be accepted. If EK3_GLITCH_RAD set to 0 the velocity innovations will be clipped instead of rejected if they exceed the gate size and a smaller value of EK3_VEL_I_GATE not exceeding 300 is recommended to limit the effect of GPS transient errors.
EK3_VEL_I_GATE.name: GPS velocity innovation gate size

EK3_VIS_VERR_MAX.desc: This is the 1-STD odometry velocity observation error that will be assumed when minimum quality is reported by the sensor. When quality is between max and min, the error will be calculated using linear interpolation between VIS_VERR_MIN and VIS_VERR_MAX.
EK3_VIS_VERR_MAX.name: Visual odometry maximum velocity error

EK3_VIS_VERR_MIN.desc: This is the 1-STD odometry velocity observation error that will be assumed when maximum quality is reported by the sensor. When quality is between max and min, the error will be calculated using linear interpolation between VIS_VERR_MIN and VIS_VERR_MAX.
EK3_VIS_VERR_MIN.name: Visual odometry minimum velocity error

EK3_WENC_VERR.desc: This is the 1-STD odometry velocity observation error that will be assumed when wheel encoder data is being fused.
EK3_WENC_VERR.name: Wheel odometry velocity error

EK3_WIND_PSCALE.desc: This controls how much the process noise on the wind states is increased when gaining or losing altitude to take into account changes in wind speed and direction with altitude. Increasing this parameter increases how rapidly the wind states adapt when changing altitude, but does make wind velocity estimation noiser.
EK3_WIND_PSCALE.name: Height rate to wind process noise scaler

EK3_WIND_PSCALE.desc: This controls how much the process noise on the wind states is increased when gaining or losing altitude to take into account changes in wind speed and direction with altitude. Increasing this parameter increases how rapidly the wind states adapt when changing altitude, but does make wind velocity estimation noiser.
EK3_WIND_PSCALE.name: Height rate to wind process noise scaler

EK3_WIND_P_NSE.desc: This state process noise controls the growth of wind state error estimates. Increasing it makes wind estimation faster and noisier.
EK3_WIND_P_NSE.name: Wind velocity process noise (m/s^2)

EK3_WIND_P_NSE.desc: This state process noise controls the growth of wind state error estimates. Increasing it makes wind estimation faster and noisier.
EK3_WIND_P_NSE.name: Wind velocity process noise (m/s^2)

EK3_YAW_I_GATE.desc: This sets the percentage number of standard deviations applied to the magnetometer yaw measurement innovation consistency check. Decreasing it makes it more likely that good measurements will be rejected. Increasing it makes it more likely that bad measurements will be accepted.
EK3_YAW_I_GATE.name: Yaw measurement gate size

EK3_YAW_M_NSE.desc: This is the RMS value of noise in yaw measurements from the magnetometer. Increasing it reduces the weighting on these measurements.
EK3_YAW_M_NSE.name: Yaw measurement noise (rad)

ENABLE.desc: When set to 0 this script will not run. When set to 1 this script will run.
ENABLE.name: Enable this script

ESC_HW_OFS.desc: Motor number offset of first ESC
ESC_HW_OFS.name: Hobbywing ESC motor offset

ESC_HW_POLES.desc: Number of motor poles for eRPM scaling
ESC_HW_POLES.name: Hobbywing ESC motor poles

ESC_TLM_MAV_OFS.desc: Offset to apply to ESC numbers when reporting as ESC_TELEMETRY packets over MAVLink. This allows high numbered motors to be displayed as low numbered ESCs for convenience on GCS displays. A value of 4 would send ESC on output 5 as ESC number 1 in ESC_TELEMETRY packets
ESC_TLM_MAV_OFS.name: ESC Telemetry mavlink offset

ESRC_EXTN_QUAL.desc: ExternalNav may be used if quality is above this threshold
ESRC_EXTN_QUAL.name: EKF Source ExternalNav Quality Threshold

ESRC_EXTN_THRESH.desc: ExternalNav may be used if innovations are below this threshold
ESRC_EXTN_THRESH.name: EKF Source ExternalNav Innovation Threshold

ESRC_FLOW_QUAL.desc: OpticalFlow may be used if quality is above this threshold
ESRC_FLOW_QUAL.name: EKF Source OpticalFlow Quality Threshold

ESRC_FLOW_THRESH.desc: OpticalFlow may be used if innovations are below this threshold
ESRC_FLOW_THRESH.name: EKF Source OpticalFlow Innovation Threshold

ESRC_RNGFND_MAX.desc: OpticalFlow may be used if rangefinder distance is below this threshold
ESRC_RNGFND_MAX.name: EKF Source Rangefinder Max

FENCE_ALT_MAX.name: Fence Maximum Altitude

FENCE_ALT_MAX_TP.name: Altitude max frame type

FENCE_ALT_MIN.desc: Minimum altitude allowed before geofence triggers

FENCE_ALT_MIN_TP.desc: The altitude reference frame for the minimum altitude fence. Can be AMSL, home-relative, origin relative or AGL.

FENCE_MARGIN.desc: Distance that autopilot's should maintain from the fence to avoid a breach
FENCE_MARGIN.name: Fence Margin

FENCE_MARGIN_XY.desc: Distance that autopilot's should maintain from the fence in the horizontal plane to avoid a breach. If set to 0 then FENCE_MARGIN is used.
FENCE_MARGIN_XY.name: Fence Horizontal Margin

FENCE_NTF_FREQ.desc: When bit 2 of FENCE_OPTIONS is set this parameter controls the frequency of margin breach notifications. If set to 0 only new margin breaches are notified.
FENCE_NTF_FREQ.name: Fence margin notification frequency in hz

bits: Disable mode change following fence action until fence breach is cleared
FENCE_OPTIONS.desc: When bit 0 is set disable mode change following fence action until fence breach is cleared. When bit 1 is set the allowable flight areas is the union of all polygon and circle fence areas instead of the intersection, which means a fence breach occurs only if you are outside all of the fence areas.

FENCE_RADIUS.desc: Circle fence radius which when breached will cause an RTL
FENCE_RADIUS.name: Circular Fence Radius

FENCE_TOTAL.desc: Number of polygon points saved in eeprom (do not update manually)
FENCE_TOTAL.name: Fence polygon point total

FFT_ATT_REF.desc: FFT attenuation level in dB for bandwidth calculation and peak detection. The bandwidth is calculated by comparing peak power output with the attenuated version. The default of 15 has shown to be a good compromise in both simulations and real flight.
FFT_ATT_REF.name: FFT attenuation for bandwidth calculation

FFT_BW_HOVER.desc: FFT learned bandwidth at hover for the attenuation frequencies.
FFT_BW_HOVER.name: FFT learned bandwidth at hover

FFT_HMNC_FIT.desc: FFT harmonic fit frequency threshold percentage at which a signal of the appropriate frequency is determined to be the harmonic of another. Signals that have a harmonic relationship that varies at most by this percentage are considered harmonics of each other for the purpose of selecting the harmonic notch frequency. If a match is found then the lower frequency harmonic is always used as the basis for the dynamic harmonic notch. A value of zero completely disables harmonic matching.
FFT_HMNC_FIT.name: FFT harmonic fit frequency threshold

FFT_HMNC_PEAK.desc: The FFT harmonic peak target that should be returned by FTN1.PkAvg. The resulting value will be used by the harmonic notch if configured to track the FFT frequency. By default the appropriate peak is auto-detected based on the harmonic fit between peaks and the energy-weighted average frequency on roll on pitch is used. Setting this to 1 will always target the highest energy peak. Setting this to 2 will target the highest energy peak that is lower in frequency than the highest energy peak. Setting this to 3 will target the highest energy peak that is higher in frequency than the highest energy peak. Setting this to 4 will target the highest energy peak on the roll axis only and only the roll frequency will be used (some vehicles have a much more pronounced peak on roll). Setting this to 5 will target the highest energy peak on the pitch axis only and only the pitch frequency will be used (some vehicles have a much more pronounced peak on roll).
FFT_HMNC_PEAK.name: FFT harmonic peak target

FFT_MAXHZ.desc: Upper bound of FFT frequency detection in Hz. On smaller vehicles the maximum motor frequency is likely to be significantly higher than for larger vehicles.
FFT_MAXHZ.name: Maximum Frequency

FFT_MINHZ.desc: Lower bound of FFT frequency detection in Hz. On larger vehicles the minimum motor frequency is likely to be significantly lower than for smaller vehicles.
FFT_MINHZ.name: Minimum Frequency

FFT_NUM_FRAMES.desc: Number of output frequency frames to retain and average in order to calculate final frequencies. Averaging output frames can drastically reduce noise and jitter at the cost of latency as long as the input is stable. The default is to perform no averaging. For rapidly changing frequencies (e.g. smaller aircraft) fewer frames should be averaged.
FFT_NUM_FRAMES.name: FFT output frames to retain and average

FFT_OPTIONS.desc: FFT configuration options. Values: 1:Apply the FFT *after* the filter bank,2:Check noise at the motor frequencies using ESC data as a reference
FFT_OPTIONS.name: FFT options

FFT_SAMPLE_MODE.desc: Sampling mode (and therefore rate). 0: Gyro rate sampling, 1: Fast loop rate sampling, 2: Fast loop rate / 2 sampling, 3: Fast loop rate / 3 sampling. Takes effect on reboot.
FFT_SAMPLE_MODE.name: Sample Mode

FFT_SNR_REF.desc: FFT SNR reference threshold in dB at which a signal is determined to be present.
FFT_SNR_REF.name: FFT SNR reference threshold

FFT_THR_REF.desc: FFT learned thrust reference for the hover frequency and FFT minimum frequency.
FFT_THR_REF.name: FFT learned thrust reference

FFT_WINDOW_OLAP.desc: Percentage of window to be overlapped before another frame is process. Takes effect on reboot. A good default is 50% overlap. Higher overlap results in more processed frames but not necessarily more temporal resolution. Lower overlap results in lost information at the frame edges.
FFT_WINDOW_OLAP.name: FFT window overlap

FFT_WINDOW_SIZE.desc: Size of window to be used in FFT calculations. Takes effect on reboot. Must be a power of 2 and between 32 and 512. Larger windows give greater frequency resolution but poorer time resolution, consume more CPU time and may not be appropriate for all vehicles. Time and frequency resolution are given by the sample-rate / window-size. Windows of 256 are only really recommended for F7 class boards, windows of 512 or more H7 class.
FFT_WINDOW_SIZE.name: FFT window size
