FILT8_NOTCH_Q.desc: Notch Filter quality factor given by the notch centre frequency divided by its bandwidth.
FILT8_NOTCH_Q.name: Notch Filter quality factor

FLOW_ADDR.desc: This is used to select between multiple possible I2C addresses for some sensor types. For PX4Flow you can choose 0 to 7 for the 8 possible addresses on the I2C bus.
FLOW_ADDR.name: Address on the bus

FLOW_FXSCALER.desc: This sets the parts per thousand scale factor correction applied to the flow sensor X axis optical rate. It can be used to correct for variations in effective focal length. Each positive increment of 1 increases the scale factor applied to the X axis optical flow reading by 0.1%. Negative values reduce the scale factor.
FLOW_FXSCALER.name: X axis optical flow scale factor correction

FLOW_FXSCALER.desc: This sets the parts per thousand scale factor correction applied to the flow sensor X axis optical rate. It can be used to correct for variations in effective focal length. Each positive increment of 1 increases the scale factor applied to the X axis optical flow reading by 0.1%. Negative values reduce the scale factor.
FLOW_FXSCALER.name: X axis optical flow scale factor correction

FLOW_FYSCALER.desc: This sets the parts per thousand scale factor correction applied to the flow sensor Y axis optical rate. It can be used to correct for variations in effective focal length. Each positive increment of 1 increases the scale factor applied to the Y axis optical flow reading by 0.1%. Negative values reduce the scale factor.
FLOW_FYSCALER.name: Y axis optical flow scale factor correction

FLOW_FYSCALER.desc: This sets the parts per thousand scale factor correction applied to the flow sensor Y axis optical rate. It can be used to correct for variations in effective focal length. Each positive increment of 1 increases the scale factor applied to the Y axis optical flow reading by 0.1%. Negative values reduce the scale factor.
FLOW_FYSCALER.name: Y axis optical flow scale factor correction

FLOW_HGT_OVR.desc: This is used in rover vehicles, where the sensor is a fixed height above the ground
FLOW_HGT_OVR.name: Height override of sensor above ground

FLOW_OPTIONS.desc: Optical flow options. Bit 0 should be set if the sensor is stabilised (e.g. mounted on a gimbal)
FLOW_OPTIONS.name: Optical flow options

FLOW_ORIENT_YAW.desc: Specifies the number of centi-degrees that the flow sensor is yawed relative to the vehicle. A sensor with its X-axis pointing to the right of the vehicle X axis has a positive yaw angle.
FLOW_ORIENT_YAW.name: Flow sensor yaw alignment

FLOW_POS_X.desc: X position of the optical flow sensor focal point in body frame. Positive X is forward of the origin.
FLOW_POS_X.name: X position offset

FLOW_POS_Y.desc: Y position of the optical flow sensor focal point in body frame. Positive Y is to the right of the origin.
FLOW_POS_Y.name: Y position offset

FLOW_POS_Z.desc: Z position of the optical flow sensor focal point in body frame. Positive Z is down from the origin.
FLOW_POS_Z.name: Z position offset

FLTMODE_GCSBLOCK.desc: Bitmask of flight modes to disable for GCS selection. Mode can still be accessed via RC or failsafe.
FLTMODE_GCSBLOCK.name: Flight mode block from GCS

FOLLP_ACT_FN.desc: Setting an RC channel's _OPTION to this value will use it for Plane Follow enable/disable
FOLLP_ACT_FN.name: Plane Follow Scripting ActivationFunction

FOLLP_ALT.desc: When non zero, this altitude value (in FOLL_ALT_TYPE frame) overrides the value sent by the target vehicle
FOLLP_ALT.name: Plane Follow Scripting Altitude Override

FOLLP_DIST_CLOSE.desc: When closer than this distance assume we track by heading
FOLLP_DIST_CLOSE.name: Plane Follow Scripting Close Distance

FOLLP_D_D.desc: D gain for the speed PID controller distance component
FOLLP_D_D.name: Plane Follow Scripting distance D gain

FOLLP_D_I.desc: I gain for the speed PID distance component
FOLLP_D_I.name: Plane Follow Scripting distance I gain

FOLLP_D_P.desc: P gain for the speed PID controller distance component
FOLLP_D_P.name: Plane Follow Scripting distance P gain

FOLLP_EXIT_MODE.desc: Mode to switch to when follow mode is exited normally
FOLLP_EXIT_MODE.name: Plane Follow exit mode

FOLLP_FAIL_MODE.desc: Mode to switch to if the target is lost (no signal or > FOLL_DIST_MAX).
FOLLP_FAIL_MODE.name: Plane Follow lost target mode

FOLLP_LkAHD.desc: Time to "lookahead" when calculating distance errors
FOLLP_LkAHD.name: Plane Follow Lookahead seconds

FOLLP_OVRSHT_DEG.desc: If the target is greater than this many degrees left or right, assume an overshoot
FOLLP_OVRSHT_DEG.name: Plane Follow Scripting Overshoot Angle

FOLLP_REFRESH.desc: refresh rate for Plane Follow updates
FOLLP_REFRESH.name: Plane Follow refresh rate

FOLLP_SIM_TLF_FN.desc: Set this switch to simulate losing telemetry from the other vehicle
FOLLP_SIM_TLF_FN.name: Plane Follow Simulate Telemetry fail function

FOLLP_TIMEOUT.desc: How long to try reaquire a target if telemetry from the lead vehicle is lost.
FOLLP_TIMEOUT.name: Plane Follow Telemetry Timeout

FOLLP_TURN_DEG.desc: If the target is greater than this many degrees left or right, assume it's turning
FOLLP_TURN_DEG.name: Plane Follow Scripting Turn Angle

FOLLP_V_D.desc: D gain for the speed PID controller velocity component
FOLLP_V_D.name: Plane Follow Scripting speed D gain

FOLLP_V_I.desc: I gain for the speed PID controller velocity component
FOLLP_V_I.name: Plane Follow Scripting speed I gain

FOLLP_V_P.desc: P gain for the speed PID controller velocity component
FOLLP_V_P.name: Plane Follow Scripting speed P gain

FOLLP_WIDE_TURNS.desc: Use wide turns when following a turning target. Alternative is "cutting the corner"
FOLLP_WIDE_TURNS.name: Plane Follow Scripting Wide Turns

FOLLP_XT_D.desc: D term for the crosstrack/heading PID controller
FOLLP_XT_D.name: Plane Follow crosstrack PID controller D term

FOLLP_XT_I.desc: I term for the crosstrack/heading PID controller
FOLLP_XT_I.name: Plane Follow crosstrack PID controller I term

FOLLP_XT_MAX.name: Plane Follow crosstrack PID controller maximum correction

FOLLP_XT_P.desc: P term for the crosstrack/heading PID controller
FOLLP_XT_P.name: Plane Follow crosstrack PID controller P term

FOLL_ACCEL_D.desc: Acceleration limit of the vertical kinematic path generation used to determine how quickly the estimate varies in velocity
FOLL_ACCEL_D.name: Acceleration limit for the vertical kinematic input shaping

FOLL_ACCEL_H.desc: Angular acceleration limit of the heading kinematic path generation used to determine how quickly the estimate varies in angular velocity
FOLL_ACCEL_H.name: Angular acceleration limit for the heading kinematic input shaping

FOLL_ACCEL_NE.desc: Acceleration limit of the horizontal kinematic path generation used to determine how quickly the estimate varies in velocity
FOLL_ACCEL_NE.name: Acceleration limit for the horizontal kinematic input shaping

FOLL_DIST_MAX.desc: Follow distance maximum. targets further than this will be ignored
FOLL_DIST_MAX.name: Follow distance maximum

FOLL_DIST_MAX.desc: Follow distance maximum. If exceeded, the follow estimate will be considered invalid. If zero there is no maximum.
FOLL_DIST_MAX.name: Follow distance maximum

FOLL_JERK_D.desc: Jerk limit of the vertical kinematic path generation used to determine how quickly the estimate varies in acceleration
FOLL_JERK_D.name: Jerk limit for the vertical kinematic input shaping

FOLL_JERK_H.desc: Angular jerk limit of the heading kinematic path generation used to determine how quickly the estimate varies in angular acceleration
FOLL_JERK_H.name: Angular jerk limit for the heading kinematic input shaping

FOLL_JERK_NE.desc: Jerk limit of the horizontal kinematic path generation used to determine how quickly the estimate varies in acceleration
FOLL_JERK_NE.name: Jerk limit for the horizontal kinematic input shaping

FOLL_OFS_X.desc: Follow offsets in meters north/forward. If positive, this vehicle fly ahead or north of lead vehicle. Depends on FOLL_OFS_TYPE
FOLL_OFS_X.name: Follow offsets in meters north/forward

FOLL_OFS_Y.desc: Follow offsets in meters east/right. If positive, this vehicle will fly to the right or east of lead vehicle. Depends on FOLL_OFS_TYPE
FOLL_OFS_Y.name: Follow offsets in meters east/right

FOLL_OFS_Z.desc: Follow offsets in meters down. If positive, this vehicle will fly below the lead vehicle
FOLL_OFS_Z.name: Follow offsets in meters down

FOLL_POS_P.desc: Follow position error P gain. Converts the difference between desired vertical speed and actual speed into a desired acceleration that is passed to the throttle acceleration controller
FOLL_POS_P.name: Follow position error P gain

FOLL_SYSID.desc: Follow target's mavlink system id. Zero means no target has been selected and following is inactive.
FOLL_SYSID.name: Follow target's mavlink system id

FOLL_SYSID.desc: Follow target's mavlink system id. Zero means no target has been selected and following is inactive.
FOLL_SYSID.name: Follow target's mavlink system id

FOLL_TIMEOUT.desc: Follow position update from lead - timeout after x seconds

FOLT_MAV_CHAN.name: Follow Target Send MAVLink Channel

FRSKY_OPTIONS.name: FRSky Telemetry Options

FRSKY_UPLINK_ID.name: Uplink sensor id

FS_GCS_ENABLE.desc: Enable ground control station telemetry failsafe. When enabled the Rover will execute the FS_ACTION when it fails to receive MAVLink heartbeat packets for FS_TIMEOUT seconds.
FS_GCS_ENABLE.name: GCS failsafe enable
values: Enabled Continue with Mission in Auto

FS_GCS_TIMEOUT.desc: Timeout before triggering the GCS failsafe
FS_GCS_TIMEOUT.name: GCS failsafe timeout

FS_THR_ENABLE.desc: The throttle failsafe allows you to configure a software failsafe activated by a setting on the throttle input channel to a low value. This can be used to detect the RC transmitter going out of range. Failsafe will be triggered when the throttle channel goes below the FS_THR_VALUE for FS_TIMEOUT seconds.
FS_THR_ENABLE.name: Throttle Failsafe Enable
values: Enabled Continue with Mission in Auto

FS_THR_ENABLE.desc: The throttle failsafe allows you to configure a software failsafe activated by a setting on the throttle input channel to a low value. This can be used to detect the RC transmitter going out of range. Failsafe will be triggered when the throttle channel reaches the FS_THR_VALUE, or goes below it, for FS_TIMEOUT seconds.
FS_THR_ENABLE.name: Throttle Failsafe Enable
values: Enabled Continue with Mission in Auto

FS_THR_VALUE.desc: The PWM level on the throttle channel below which throttle failsafe triggers.
FS_THR_VALUE.name: Throttle Failsafe Value

FS_THR_VALUE.desc: The PWM level on the throttle channel at or below which throttle failsafe triggers.
FS_THR_VALUE.name: Throttle Failsafe Value

FS_TIMEOUT.desc: The time in seconds that a failsafe condition must persist before the failsafe action is triggered

GND_ALT_OFFSET.desc: altitude offset in meters added to barometric altitude. This is used to allow for automatic adjustment of the base barometric altitude by a ground station equipped with a barometer. The value is added to the barometric altitude read by the aircraft. It is automatically reset to 0 when the barometer is calibrated on each reboot or when a preflight calibration is performed.
GND_ALT_OFFSET.name: altitude offset

GND_EXT_BUS.desc: This selects the bus number for looking for an I2C barometer. When set to -1 it will probe all external i2c buses based on the GND_PROBE_EXT parameter.
GND_EXT_BUS.name: External baro bus

GND_FLTR_RNG.desc: This sets the range around the average value that new samples must be within to be accepted. This can help reduce the impact of noise on sensors that are on long I2C cables. The value is a percentage from the average value. A value of zero disables this filter.
GND_FLTR_RNG.name: Range in which sample is accepted

GND_PRIMARY.desc: This selects which barometer will be the primary if multiple barometers are found
GND_PRIMARY.name: Primary barometer

GND_PROBE_EXT.desc: This sets which types of external i2c barometer to look for. It is a bitmask of barometer types. The I2C buses to probe is based on GND_EXT_BUS. If GND_EXT_BUS is -1 then it will probe all external buses, otherwise it will probe just the bus number given in GND_EXT_BUS.
GND_PROBE_EXT.name: External barometers to probe

GND_SPEC_GRAV.desc: This sets the specific gravity of the fluid when flying an underwater ROV.
GND_SPEC_GRAV.name: Specific Gravity (For water depth measurement)

GND_TEMP.desc: User provided ambient ground temperature in degrees Celsius. This is used to improve the calculation of the altitude the vehicle is at. This parameter is not persistent and will be reset to 0 every time the vehicle is rebooted. A value of 0 means use the internal measurement ambient temperature.
GND_TEMP.name: ground temperature

INS_HNTC2_ESCMSK.desc: Bitmask of ESC channels to use in ESC Telemetry mode. 0 uses all available ESCs.

INS_HNTC2_FM_RAT.desc: The minimum ratio below the configured frequency to take throttle based notch filters when flying at a throttle level below the reference throttle. Note that lower frequency notch filters will have more phase lag. If you want throttle based notch filtering to be effective at a throttle up to 30% below the configured notch frequency then set this parameter to 0.7. The default of 1.0 means the notch will not go below the frequency in the FREQ parameter.
INS_HNTC2_FM_RAT.name: Throttle notch min freqency ratio

INS_HNTC2_FM_RAT.desc: The minimum ratio below the configured frequency to take throttle based notch filters when flying at a throttle level below the reference throttle. INS_HNTC2_FREQ.desc: Harmonic Notch Filter base center frequency in Hz. This should be set at most half the backend gyro rate (which is typically 1Khz). For helicopters using RPM sensor to dynamically set the notch frequency, use this parameter to provide a lower limit to the dynamic notch filter. Recommend setting it to half the operating rotor speed in Hz.

This should always be set lower than half the backend gyro rate (which is typically 1Khz).
INS_HNTC2_FREQ.name: Harmonic Notch Filter base frequency

INS_HNTC2_OPTS.desc: Harmonic Notch Filter options. Double-notches can provide deeper attenuation across a wider bandwidth than single notches and are suitable for larger aircraft. Dynamic harmonics attaches a harmonic notch to each detected noise frequency instead of simply being multiples of the base frequency, in the case of FFT it will attach notches to each of three detected noise peaks, in the case of ESC it will attach notches to each of four motor RPM values. Loop rate update changes the notch center frequency at the scheduler loop rate rather than at the default of 200Hz.
INS_HNTC2_OPTS.name: Harmonic Notch Filter options

INS_HNTC2_OPTS.desc: Harmonic Notch Filter options. Triple and double-notches can provide deeper attenuation across a wider bandwidth with reduced latency than single notches and are suitable for larger aircraft. Dynamic harmonics attaches a harmonic notch to each detected noise frequency instead of simply being multiples of the base frequency, in the case of FFT it will attach notches to each of three detected noise peaks, in the case of ESC it will attach notches to each of four motor RPM values. Loop rate update changes the notch center frequency at the scheduler loop rate rather than at the default of 200Hz. If both double and triple notches are specified only double notches will take effect.
INS_HNTC2_OPTS.name: Harmonic Notch Filter options

INS_HNTC2_REF.desc: A reference value of zero disables dynamic updates on the Harmonic Notch Filter and a positive value enables dynamic updates on the Harmonic Notch Filter. For throttle-based scaling, this parameter is the reference value associated with the specified frequency to facilitate frequency scaling of the Harmonic Notch Filter. For RPM and ESC telemetry based tracking, this parameter is set to 1 to enable the Harmonic Notch Filter using the RPM sensor or ESC telemetry set to measure rotor speed. The sensor data is converted to Hz automatically for use in the Harmonic Notch Filter. This reference value may also be used to scale the sensor data, if required. For example, rpm sensor data is required to measure heli motor RPM. Therefore the reference value can be used to scale the RPM sensor to the rotor RPM.

INS_HNTC4_REF.desc: A reference value of zero disables dynamic updates on the Harmonic Notch Filter and a positive value enables dynamic updates on the Harmonic Notch Filter. For throttle-based scaling, this parameter is the reference value associated with the specified frequency to facilitate frequency scaling of the Harmonic Notch Filter. For RPM and ESC telemetry based tracking, this parameter is set to 1 to enable the Harmonic Notch Filter using the RPM sensor or ESC telemetry set to measure rotor speed. The sensor data is converted to Hz automatically for use in the Harmonic Notch Filter. This reference value may also be used to scale the sensor data, if required. For example, rpm sensor data is required to measure heli motor RPM. Therefore the reference value can be used to scale the RPM sensor to the rotor RPM.
INS_HNTC4_REF.name: Harmonic Notch Filter reference value

INS_HNTCH_ATT.desc: Harmonic Notch Filter attenuation in dB
INS_HNTCH_ATT.name: Harmonic Notch Filter attenuation

INS_HNTCH_ATT.desc: Harmonic Notch Filter attenuation in dB. Values greater than 40dB will typically produce a hard notch rather than a modest attenuation of motor noise.
INS_HNTCH_ATT.name: Harmonic Notch Filter attenuation

INS_HNTCH_BW.desc: Harmonic Notch Filter bandwidth in Hz
INS_HNTCH_BW.name: Harmonic Notch Filter bandwidth

INS_HNTCH_BW.desc: Harmonic Notch Filter bandwidth in Hz. This is typically set to half the base frequency. The ratio of base frequency to bandwidth determines the notch quality factor and is fixed across harmonics.
INS_HNTCH_BW.name: Harmonic Notch Filter bandwidth

INS_HNTCH_ESCMSK.desc: Bitmask of ESC channels to use in ESC Telemetry mode. 0 uses all available ESCs.
INS_HNTCH_ESCMSK.name: Harmonic Notch Filter ESC mask

INS_HNTCH_FM_RAT.desc: The minimum ratio below the configured frequency to take throttle based notch filters when flying at a throttle level below the reference throttle. Note that lower frequency notch filters will have more phase lag. If you want throttle based notch filtering to be effective at a throttle up to 30% below the configured notch frequency then set this parameter to 0.7. The default of 1.0 means the notch will not go below the frequency in the FREQ parameter.
INS_HNTCH_FM_RAT.name: Throttle notch min freqency ratio

INS_HNTCH_FM_RAT.desc: The minimum ratio below the configured frequency to take throttle based notch filters when flying at a throttle level below the reference throttle. Note that lower frequency notch filters will have more phase lag. If you want throttle based notch filtering to be effective at a throttle up to 30% below the configured notch frequency then set this parameter to 0.7. The default of 1.0 means the notch will not go below the frequency in the FREQ parameter.
INS_HNTCH_FM_RAT.name: Throttle notch min frequency ratio

INS_HNTCH_FREQ.desc: Harmonic Notch Filter base center frequency in Hz. For helicopters using RPM sensor to dynamically set the notch frequency, use this parameter to provide a lower limit to the dynamic notch filter. Recommend setting it to half the operating rotor speed in Hz.
INS_HNTCH_FREQ.name: Harmonic Notch Filter base frequency

INS_HNTCH_FREQ.desc: Harmonic Notch Filter base center frequency in Hz. This should be set at most half the backend gyro rate (which is typically 1Khz). For helicopters using RPM sensor to dynamically set the notch frequency, use this parameter to provide a lower limit to the dynamic notch filter. Recommend setting it to half the operating rotor speed in Hz.
INS_HNTCH_FREQ.name: Harmonic Notch Filter base frequency

INS_HNTCH_FREQ.desc: Harmonic Notch Filter base center frequency in Hz. This is the center frequency for static notches, the center frequency for Throttle based notches at the reference thrust value, and the minimum limit of center frequency variation for all other notch types. This should always be set lower than half the backend gyro rate (which is typically 1Khz).
INS_HNTCH_FREQ.name: Harmonic Notch Filter base frequency

INS_HNTCH_HMNCS.desc: Bitmask of harmonic frequencies to apply Harmonic Notch Filter to. This option takes effect on the next reboot. A maximum of 3 harmonics can be used at any one time.
INS_HNTCH_HMNCS.name: Harmonic Notch Filter harmonics

INS_HNTCH_HMNCS.desc: Bitmask of harmonic frequencies to apply Harmonic Notch Filter to. This option takes effect on the next reboot. A value of 0 disables this filter. The first harmonic refers to the base frequency.

INS_HNTCH_OPTS.desc: Harmonic Notch Filter options. Double-notches can provide deeper attenuation across a wider bandwidth than single notches and are suitable for larger aircraft. Dynamic harmonics attaches a harmonic notch to each detected noise frequency instead of simply being multiples of the base frequency, in the case of FFT it will attach notches to each of three detected noise peaks, in the case of ESC it will attach notches to each of four motor RPM values. Loop rate update changes the notch center frequency at the scheduler loop rate rather than at the default of 200Hz.
INS_HNTCH_OPTS.name: Harmonic Notch Filter options

Triple and double-notches can provide deeper attenuation across a wider bandwidth with reduced latency than single notches and are suitable for larger aircraft. INS_POS1_X.desc: X position of the first IMU Accelerometer in body frame. Positive X is forward of the origin. Attention: The IMU should be located as close to the vehicle c.g. as practical so that the value of this parameter is minimised. If the IMU cannot be moved and velocity noise is a problem, a location closer to the IMU can be used as the body frame origin.

LOG_DISARMED.desc: If LOG_DISARMED is set to 1 then logging will be enabled while disarmed. This can make for very large logfiles but can help a lot when tracking down startup issues
LOG_DISARMED.name: Enable logging while disarmed

LOG_DISARMED.desc: If LOG_DISARMED is set to 1 then logging will be enabled at all times including when disarmed. Logging before arming can make for very large logfiles but can help a lot when tracking down startup issues and is necessary if logging of EKF replay data is selected via the LOG_REPLAY parameter. If LOG_DISARMED is set to 2, then logging will be enabled when disarmed, but not if a USB connection is detected. This can be used to prevent unwanted data logs being generated when the vehicle is connected via USB for log downloading or parameter changes. If LOG_DISARMED is set to 3 then logging will happen while disarmed, but if the vehicle never arms then the logs using the filesystem backend will be discarded on the next boot.
LOG_DISARMED.name: Enable logging while disarmed
values: Discard log on reboot if never armed

LOG_REPLAY.desc: If LOG_REPLAY is set to 1 then the EKF2 and EKF3 state estimators will log detailed information needed for diagnosing problems with the Kalman filter. LOG_REPLAY.name: Enable logging of information needed for Replay

MAV_GCS_SYSID.desc: This sets what MAVLink source system IDs are accepted for GCS failsafe handling, RC overrides and manual control. When MAV_GCS_SYSID_HI is less than MAV_GCS_SYSID then only this value is considered to be a GCS. When MAV_GCS_SYSID_HI is greater than or equal to MAV_GCS_SYSID then the range of values between MAV_GCS_SYSID and MAV_GCS_SYSID_HI (inclusive) are all treated as valid GCS MAVLink system IDs

NAVL1_DAMPING.desc: Damping ratio for L1 control. Increase this in increments of 0.05 if you are getting overshoot in path tracking. You should not need a value below 0.7 or above 0.85.
NAVL1_DAMPING.name: L1 control damping ratio

NAVL1_LIM_BANK.desc: The sealevel bank angle limit for a continous loiter. (Used to calculate airframe loading limits at higher altitudes). Setting to 0, will instead just scale the loiter radius directly
NAVL1_LIM_BANK.name: Loiter Radius Bank Angle Limit

NAVL1_PERIOD.desc: Period in seconds of L1 tracking loop. This parameter is the primary control for agressiveness of turns in auto mode. This needs to be larger for less responsive airframes. The default of 20 is quite conservative, but for most RC aircraft will lead to reasonable flight. For smaller more agile aircraft a value closer to 15 is appropriate, or even as low as 10 for some very agile aircraft. When tuning, change this value in small increments, as a value that is much too small (say 5 or 10 below the right value) can lead to very radical turns, and a risk of stalling.
NAVL1_PERIOD.name: L1 control period

NAVL1_XTRACK_I.desc: Crosstrack error integrator gain. This gain is applied to the crosstrack error to ensure it converges to zero. Set to zero to disable. Smaller values converge slower, higher values will cause crosstrack error oscillation.
NAVL1_XTRACK_I.name: L1 control crosstrack integrator gain

QUIK_ANGLE_MAX.desc: If while tuning the angle error goes over this limit then the tune will aborts to prevent a bad oscillation in the case of the tuning algorithm failing. If you get an error "Tuning: attitude error ABORTING" and you think it is a false positive then you can either raise this parameter or you can try increasing the QUIK_DOUBLE_TIME to do the tune more slowly. A value of zero disables this check.
QUIK_ANGLE_MAX.name: maximum angle error for tune abort

QUIK_AUTO_FILTER.desc: When enabled the PID filter settings are automatically set based on INS_GYRO_FILTER
QUIK_AUTO_FILTER.name: Quicktune auto filter enable

QUIK_AUTO_SAVE.desc: Number of seconds after completion of tune to auto-save. This is useful when using a 2 position switch for quicktune
QUIK_AUTO_SAVE.name: Quicktune auto save

QUIK_DOUBLE_TIME.desc: Time to double a tuning parameter. Raise this for a slower tune.
QUIK_DOUBLE_TIME.name: Quicktune doubling time

QUIK_GAIN_MARGIN.desc: Reduction in gain after oscillation detected. Raise this number to get a more conservative tune
QUIK_GAIN_MARGIN.name: Quicktune gain margin

QUIK_MAX_REDUCE.desc: This controls how much quicktune is allowed to lower gains from the original gains. If the vehicle already has a reasonable tune and is not oscillating then you can set this to zero to prevent gain reductions. The default of 20% is reasonable for most vehicles. Using a maximum gain reduction lowers the chance of an angle P oscillation happening if quicktune gets a false positive oscillation at a low gain, which can result in very low rate gains and a dangerous angle P oscillation.
QUIK_MAX_REDUCE.name: Quicktune maximum gain reduction

QUIK_OPTIONS.desc: Additional options. When the Two Position Switch option is enabled then a high switch position will start the tune, low will disable the tune. you should also set a QUIK_AUTO_SAVE time so that you will be able to save the tune.
QUIK_OPTIONS.name: Quicktune options

QUIK_OSC_SMAX.desc: Threshold for oscillation detection. A lower value will lead to a more conservative tune.
QUIK_OSC_SMAX.name: Quicktune oscillation rate threshold

QUIK_RC_FUNC.desc: RCn_OPTION number to use to control tuning stop/start/save
QUIK_RC_FUNC.name: Quicktune RC function

QUIK_RP_PI_RATIO.desc: Ratio between P and I gains for roll and pitch. Raise this to get a lower I gain
QUIK_RP_PI_RATIO.name: Quicktune roll/pitch PI ratio

QUIK_YAW_D_MAX.desc: Maximum value for yaw D gain
QUIK_YAW_D_MAX.name: Quicktune Yaw D max

QUIK_YAW_P_MAX.desc: Maximum value for yaw P gain
QUIK_YAW_P_MAX.name: Quicktune Yaw P max

QUIK_Y_PI_RATIO.desc: Ratio between P and I gains for yaw. Raise this to get a lower I gain
QUIK_Y_PI_RATIO.name: Quicktune Yaw PI ratio

RALLY_LIMIT_KM.desc: Maximum distance to rally point. This prevents a leftover rally point from a different airfield being used accidentally. If this is set to 0 then the closest rally point is always used.

RCMAP_PITCH.desc: Pitch channel number. This is useful when you have a RC transmitter that can't change the channel order easily. Pitch is normally on channel 2, but you can move it to any channel with this parameter. Reboot is required for changes to take effect.
RCMAP_PITCH.name: Pitch channel

RCMAP_ROLL.desc: Roll channel number. This is useful when you have a RC transmitter that can't change the channel order easily. Roll is normally on channel 1, but you can move it to any channel with this parameter. Reboot is required for changes to take effect.

RCMAP_ROLL.desc: Roll channel number. This is useful when you have a RC transmitter that can't change the channel order easily. Roll is normally on channel 1, but you can move it to any channel with this parameter. Reboot is required for changes to take effect.

RCMAP_THROTTLE.desc: Throttle channel number. This is useful when you have a RC transmitter that can't change the channel order easily. Throttle is normally on channel 3, but you can move it to any channel with this parameter. Warning APM 2.X: Changing the throttle channel could produce unexpected fail-safe results if connection between receiver and on-board PPM Encoder is lost. Disabling on-board PPM Encoder is recommended. Reboot is required for changes to take effect.
RCMAP_THROTTLE.name: Throttle channel

RNGFND1_ADDR.desc: This sets the bus address of the sensor, where applicable. Used for the I2C and UAVCAN sensors to allow for multiple sensors on different addresses.
RNGFND1_ADDR.name: Bus address of sensor

RNGFND1_ADDR.desc: This sets the bus address of the sensor, where applicable. Used for the I2C and DroneCAN sensors to allow for multiple sensors on different addresses.
RNGFND1_ADDR.name: Bus address of sensor

RNGFND1_ADDR.name: Bus address of sensor

RNGFND1_FUNCTION.desc: Control over what function is used to calculate distance. For a linear function, the distance is (voltage-offset)*scaling. For a inverted function the distance is (offset-voltage)*scaling. For a hyperbolic function the distance is scaling/(voltage-offset). The functions return the distance in meters.
RNGFND1_FUNCTION.name: Rangefinder function

RNGFND1_GNDCLEAR.desc: This parameter sets the expected range measurement(in cm) that the range finder should return when the vehicle is on the ground.
RNGFND1_GNDCLEAR.name: Distance (in cm) from the range finder to the ground

RNGFND1_GNDCLR.desc: This parameter sets the expected range measurement that the range finder should return when the vehicle is on the ground.
RNGFND1_GNDCLR.name: Distance from the range finder to the ground

RNGFND1_GRF_RATE.desc: The update rate of the sensor in Hz.
RNGFND1_GRF_RATE.name: LightWare GRF Update Rate

RNGFND1_GRF_RET.desc: Selects which single return to use.
RNGFND1_GRF_RET.name: LightWare GRF Distance Return Type

RNGFND1_GRF_ST.desc: Minimum acceptable return signal strength in dB. Returns weaker than this will be ignored. Set to 0 to disable filtering.
RNGFND1_GRF_ST.name: LightWare GRF Minimum Return Strength

RNGFND1_MAX.desc: Maximum distance in metres that rangefinder can reliably read
RNGFND1_MAX.name: Rangefinder maximum distance

RNGFND1_MAX_CM.desc: Maximum distance in centimeters that rangefinder can reliably read
RNGFND1_MAX_CM.name: Rangefinder maximum distance

RNGFND1_MIN.desc: Minimum distance in metres that rangefinder can reliably read
RNGFND1_MIN.name: Rangefinder minimum distance

RNGFND1_MIN_CM.desc: Minimum distance in centimeters that rangefinder can reliably read
RNGFND1_MIN_CM.name: Rangefinder minimum distance

RNGFND1_OFFSET.desc: Offset in volts for zero distance for analog rangefinders. Offset added to distance in centimeters for PWM lidars
RNGFND1_OFFSET.name: rangefinder offset

RNGFND1_PIN.name: Rangefinder pin

RNGFND1_PIN.desc: Analog or PWM input pin that rangefinder is connected to. Airspeed ports can be used for Analog input, AUXOUT can be used for PWM input. When using analog pin 103, the maximum value of the input in 3.3V.

RNGFND1_POS_X.name: X position offset

RNGFND1_POS_Y.desc: Y position of the rangefinder in body frame. Positive Y is to the right of the origin. Use the zero range datum point if supplied.
RNGFND1_POS_Y.name: Y position offset

RNGFND1_POS_Z.desc: Z position of the rangefinder in body frame. Positive Z is down from the origin. Use the zero range datum point if supplied.

RNGFND1_PWRRNG.name: Powersave range

RNGFND1_RECV_ID.desc: The receive ID of the CAN frames. A value of zero means all IDs are accepted.
RNGFND1_RECV_ID.name: CAN receive ID

RNGFND1_RMETRIC.desc: This parameter sets whether an analog rangefinder is ratiometric. Most analog rangefinders are ratiometric, meaning that their output voltage is influenced by the supply voltage. Some analog rangefinders (such as the SF/02) have their own internal voltage regulators so they are not ratiometric.
RNGFND1_RMETRIC.name: Ratiometric

RNGFND1_SCALING.desc: Scaling factor between rangefinder reading and distance. For the linear and inverted functions this is in meters per volt. For the hyperbolic function the units are meterVolts.

SCR_THD_PRIORITY.desc: This sets the priority of the scripting thread. This is normally set to a low priority to prevent scripts from interfering with other parts of the system. Advanced users can change this priority if scripting needs to be prioritised for realtime applications. WARNING: changing this parameter can impact the stability of your flight controller. The scipting thread priority in this parameter is chosen based on a set of system level priorities for other subsystems. It is strongly recommended that you use the lowest priority that is sufficient for your application. Note that all scripts run at the same priority, so if you raise this priority you must carefully audit all lua scripts for behaviour that does not interfere with the operation of the system.

SERIAL_PASS1.desc: This sets one side of pass-through between two serial ports. Once both sides are set then all data received on either port will be passed to the other port
SERIAL_PASS1.name: Serial passthru first port

SERIAL_PASS2.desc: This sets one side of pass-through between two serial ports. Once both sides are set then all data received on either port will be passed to the other port
SERIAL_PASS2.name: Serial passthru second port

SERIAL_PASS2.desc: This sets one side of pass-through between two serial ports. Once both sides are set then all data received on either port will be passed to the other port. This parameter is normally reset to -1 on reboot, disabling passthrough. If SERIAL_PASSTIMO is set to -1 then it is not reset on reboot.
SERIAL_PASS2.name: Serial passthru second port

SERIAL_PASSTIMO.desc: This sets a timeout for serial pass-through in seconds. When the pass-through is enabled by setting the SERIAL_PASS1 and SERIAL_PASS2 parameters then it remains in effect until no data comes from the first port for SERIAL_PASSTIMO seconds. This allows the port to revent to its normal usage (such as MAVLink connection to a GCS) when it is no longer needed. A value of 0 means no timeout.
SERIAL_PASSTIMO.name: Serial passthru timeout

SERIAL_PASSTIMO.desc: This sets a timeout for serial pass-through in seconds. When the pass-through is enabled by setting the SERIAL_PASS1 and SERIAL_PASS2 parameters then it remains in effect until no data comes from the first port for SERIAL_PASSTIMO seconds. This allows the port to revent to its normal usage (such as MAVLink connection to a GCS) when it is no longer needed. A value of 0 means no timeout. A value of -1 means no timeout and the SERIAL_PASS2 parameter is not reset on reboot.
SERIAL_PASSTIMO.name: Serial passthru timeout

SERVO_BLH_OTYPE.name: BLHeli output type override

SERVO_BLH_RVMASK.desc: Mask of channels which are reversed. This is used to configure ESCs to reverse motor direction. Note that when combined with SERVO_BLH_3DMASK this will change what direction is considered to be forward.

SERVO_BLH_TEST.desc: Setting SERVO_BLH_TEST to a motor number enables an internal test of the BLHeli ESC protocol to the corresponding ESC. The debug output is displayed on the USB console.
SERVO_BLH_TEST.name: BLHeli internal interface test

SERVO_BLH_TMOUT.desc: This sets the inactivity timeout for the BLHeli protocol in seconds. If no packets are received in this time normal MAVLink operations are resumed. A value of 0 means no timeout
SERVO_BLH_TMOUT.name: BLHeli protocol timeout

SERVO_BLH_TRATE.desc: This sets the rate in Hz for requesting telemetry from ESCs. It is the rate per ESC. Setting to zero disables telemetry requests
SERVO_BLH_TRATE.name: BLHeli telemetry rate

SERVO_DSHOT_ESC.desc: This sets the DShot ESC type for all outputs. The ESC type affects the range of DShot commands available. None means that no dshot commands will be executed.
SERVO_DSHOT_ESC.name: Servo DShot ESC type

SERVO_DSHOT_ESC.desc: This sets the DShot ESC type for all outputs. The ESC type affects the range of DShot commands available. None means that no dshot commands will be executed.
SERVO_DSHOT_ESC.name: Servo DShot ESC type

SERVO_DSHOT_ESC.desc: DShot ESC type for all outputs. The ESC type affects the range of DShot commands available and the bit widths used. None means that no dshot commands will be executed. Some ESC types support Extended DShot Telemetry (EDT) which allows telemetry other than RPM data to be returned when using bi-directional dshot. If you enable EDT you must install EDT capable firmware for correct operation.
SERVO_DSHOT_ESC.name: Servo DShot ESC type

SERVO_DSHOT_ESC.desc: DShot ESC type for all outputs. The ESC type affects the range of DShot commands available and the bit widths used. None means that no dshot commands will be executed. SERVO_DSHOT_ESC.name: Servo DShot ESC type

SERVO_DSHOT_RATE.desc: This sets the DShot output rate for all outputs as a multiple of the loop rate. 0 sets the output rate to be fixed at 1Khz for low loop rates. This value should never be set below 500Hz.
SERVO_DSHOT_RATE.name: Servo DShot output rate

SERVO_VOLZ_MASK.name: Channel Bitmask

SERVO_VOLZ_MASK.desc: Enable of volz servo protocol to specific channels
SERVO_VOLZ_MASK.name: Channel Bitmask

SERVO_VOLZ_RANGE.desc: Range to map between 1000 and 2000 PWM. Default value of 200 gives full +-100 deg range of extended position command. This results in 0.2 deg movement per US change in PWM. If the full range is not needed it can be reduced to increase resolution. 40 deg range gives 0.04 deg movement per US change in PWM, this is higher resolution than possible with the VOLZ protocol so further reduction in range will not improve resolution. Reduced range does allow PWMs outside the 1000 to 2000 range, with 40 deg range 750 PWM results in a angle of -30 deg, 2250 would be +30 deg. This is still limited by the 200 deg maximum range of the actuator.
SERVO_VOLZ_RANGE.name: Range of travel

SHIP_AUTO_OFS.desc: Settings this parameter to one triggers an automatic follow offset calculation based on current position of the vehicle and the landing target. NOTE: This parameter will auto-reset to zero once the offset has been calculated.
SHIP_AUTO_OFS.name: Ship automatic offset trigger

SHIP_LAND_ANGLE.desc: Angle from the stern of the ship for landing approach. Use this to ensure that on a go-around that ship superstructure and cables are avoided. A value of zero means to approach from the rear of the ship. A value of 90 means the landing will approach from the port (left) side of the ship. A value of -90 will mean approaching from the starboard (right) side of the ship. A value of 180 will approach from the bow of the ship. This parameter is combined with the sign of the RTL_RADIUS parameter to determine the holdoff pattern. If RTL_RADIUS is positive then a clockwise loiter is performed, if RTL_RADIUS is negative then a counter-clockwise loiter is used.
SHIP_LAND_ANGLE.name: Ship landing angle

SIM_BATT_VOLTAGE.desc: Simulated battery resting voltage (no load sag). Defaults to and clipped to the battery model's maximum voltage. Changes re-initialize the state of charge, and values below the maximum indicate a partially-charged battery. For batteries with unlimited capacity, see `SIM_BATT_CAP_AH`. Value ignored when receiving battery state updates from an external source.

SRTL_ACCURACY.name: SmartRTL accuracy

SRTL_POINTS.name: SmartRTL maximum number of points on path

STAT_BOOTCNT.desc: Number of times board has been booted
STAT_BOOTCNT.name: Boot Count

STAT_DISTFLWN.desc: Estimate of total distance flown since statistics reset
STAT_DISTFLWN.name: Total Distance Flown

STAT_RESET.desc: Seconds since January 1st 2016 (Unix epoch+1451606400) since statistics reset (set to 0 to reset statistics)
STAT_RESET.name: Statistics Reset Time

STAT_RESET.name: Statistics Reset Time

STICK_MIXING.desc: When enabled, this adds steering user stick input in auto modes, allowing the user to have some degree of control without changing modes.
STICK_MIXING.name: Stick Mixing

SYSID_ENFORCE.desc: This controls whether packets from other than the expected GCS system ID will be accepted
SYSID_ENFORCE.name: GCS sysid enforcement

SYSID_MYGCS.desc: The identifier of the ground station in the MAVLink protocol. Don't change this unless you also modify the ground station to match.
SYSID_MYGCS.name: MAVLink ground station ID

SYSID_MYGCS.name: MAVLink ground station ID

SYSID_THISMAV.desc: Allows setting an individual MAVLink system id for this vehicle to distinguish it from others on the same network
SYSID_THISMAV.name: MAVLink system ID of this vehicle

SYSID_THIS_MAV.desc: Allows setting an individual MAVLink system id for this vehicle to distinguish it from others on the same network
SYSID_THIS_MAV.name: MAVLink system ID of this vehicle

TA_ACT_FN.desc: Setting an RC channel's _OPTION to this value will use it for Terrain Avoidance enable/disable
TA_ACT_FN.name: Activation Function for Terrain Avoidance

TA_ALT_MAX.desc: This is a limit on how high the terrain avoidane will take the vehicle. It acts a failsafe to prevent vertical flyaways.
TA_ALT_MAX.name: ceiling for pitching/quading

TA_CMTC_ENABLE.desc: Whether to enable Can't Make That Climb while running Terrain Avoidance
TA_CMTC_ENABLE.name: CMTC Enable

TA_CMTC_HGT.desc: The minimum Height above terrain to maintain when following an AUTO mission or RTL. If zero(0) use TA_PTCH_DOW_MIN.
TA_CMTC_HGT.name: CMTC Height

TA_CMTC_RAD.desc: Use this radius for the loiter when trying to gain altitude. If not set or <=0 use WP_LOITER_RAD
TA_CMTC_RAD.name: CMTC loiter radius

TA_GSP_AIRBRAKE.desc: This is the limit for triggering airbrake to slow groundspeed as a difference between the airspeed and groundspeed. -1 for disabled.
TA_GSP_AIRBRAKE.name: Groudspeed Airbrake limt

TA_GSP_MAX.desc: This is a limit on how fast in groundspeeed terrain avoidance will take the vehicle. This is to allow for reliable sensor readings. -1 for disabled.
TA_GSP_MAX.name: Maximum Groundspeed

TA_HOME_DIST.desc: Terrain avoidance will not be applied if the vehicle is less than this distance from home
TA_HOME_DIST.name: safe distance around home

TA_PTCH_DWN_MIN.desc: If the downward distance is less than this value then start Pitching up to gain altitude.
TA_PTCH_DWN_MIN.name: down distance minimum for Pitching

TA_PTCH_FWD_MIN.desc: If the farwardward distance is less than this value then start Pitching up to gain altitude.
TA_PTCH_FWD_MIN.name: forward distance minimum for Pitching

TA_PTCH_GSP_MIN.desc: Minimum Groundspeed (not airspeed) to be flying for Pitching to be used.
TA_PTCH_GSP_MIN.name: minimum ground speed for Pitching

TA_PTCH_TIMEOUT.desc: Minimum down or forward distance must be triggered for more than this many seconds to start Pitching
TA_PTCH_TIMEOUT.name: timeout Pitching

TA_QUAD_DWN_MIN.desc: If the downward distance is less than this value then start Quading up to gain altitude.
TA_QUAD_DWN_MIN.name: Downward distance minimum Quading

TA_QUAD_FWD_MIN.desc: If the farwardward distance is less than this value then start Quading up to gain altitude.
TA_QUAD_FWD_MIN.name: minimum forward distance for Quading

TELEM_DELAY.desc: The amount of time (in seconds) to delay radio telemetry to prevent an Xbee bricking on power up
TELEM_DELAY.name: Telemetry startup delay

WRC_RATE_D.desc: Wheel rate control D gain. Compensates for short-term change in desired rate vs actual
WRC_RATE_D.name: Wheel rate control D gain

WRC_RATE_D_FF.desc: FF D Gain which produces an output that is proportional to the rate of change of the error
WRC_RATE_D_FF.name: Wheel rate Derivative FeedForward Gain

WRC_RATE_FF.desc: Wheel rate control feed forward gain. Desired rate (in radians/sec) is multiplied by this constant and output to output (in the range -1 to +1)
WRC_RATE_FF.name: Wheel rate control feed forward gain

WRC_RATE_FILT.desc: Wheel rate control input filter. Lower values reduce noise but add delay.
WRC_RATE_FILT.name: Wheel rate control filter frequency

WRC_RATE_FLTD.desc: Wheel rate control derivative frequency in Hz
WRC_RATE_FLTD.name: Wheel rate control derivative frequency in Hz

WRC_RATE_FLTE.desc: Wheel rate control error frequency in Hz
WRC_RATE_FLTE.name: Wheel rate control error frequency in Hz

WRC_RATE_FLTT.desc: Wheel rate control target frequency in Hz
WRC_RATE_FLTT.name: Wheel rate control target frequency in Hz

WRC_RATE_I.desc: Wheel rate control I gain. Corrects long term error between the desired rate (in rad/s) and actual
WRC_RATE_I.name: Wheel rate control I gain

WRC_RATE_IMAX.desc: Wheel rate control I gain maximum. Constrains the output (range -1 to +1) that the I term will generate
WRC_RATE_IMAX.name: Wheel rate control I gain maximum

WRC_RATE_NEF.desc: Wheel rate Error notch filter index
WRC_RATE_NEF.name: Wheel rate Error notch filter index

WRC_RATE_NEF.desc: Wheel rate Error notch filter index, zero disables
WRC_RATE_NEF.name: Wheel rate Error notch filter index

WRC_RATE_NTF.desc: Wheel rate Target notch filter index
WRC_RATE_NTF.name: Wheel rate Target notch filter index

WRC_RATE_NTF.desc: Wheel rate Target notch filter index, zero disables
WRC_RATE_NTF.name: Wheel rate Target notch filter index

WRC_RATE_P.desc: Wheel rate control P gain. Converts rate error (in radians/sec) to output (in the range -1 to +1)
WRC_RATE_P.name: Wheel rate control P gain

WRC_RATE_PDMX.desc: Wheel rate control PD sum maximum. The maximum/minimum value that the sum of the P and D term can output
WRC_RATE_PDMX.name: Wheel rate control PD sum maximum

WRC_RATE_SMAX.desc: Sets an upper limit on the slew rate produced by the combined P and D gains. If the amplitude of the control action produced by the rate feedback exceeds this value, then the D+P gain is reduced to respect the limit. This limits the amplitude of high frequency oscillations caused by an excessive gain. The limit should be set to no more than 25% of the actuators maximum slew rate to allow for load effects. Note: The gain will not be reduced to less than 10% of the nominal value. A value of zero will disable this feature.
WRC_RATE_SMAX.name: Wheel rate slew rate limit
